14	## Structural — true in every register
15	
16	- **Palette:** 8–10 named tokens, oklch where the stack allows. Exactly ONE
17	  saturated accent, deployed at display scale (drop caps, giant prices, glyphs, a
18	  drawn form) and never as fill on a small control.
19	- **Hierarchy through scale, not decoration.** Display clamp() with leading
20	  0.9–0.95; body measure capped in ch. No shadow stacks, no gradient borders.
21	- **Hairlines separate; planes do not.**
22	- **Stagger:** paired columns never top-align.
23	- **Every open column carries weight** — a display numeral, a stat, an image, or a
24	  full-height rule. Otherwise close it.
25	- **At least three distinct section anatomies** per page.
26	- **One tonal inversion** somewhere on the page.
27	- **Motion:** one shared reveal (translateY 28px, 1.2–1.4s,
28	  cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)), failing toward visible; plus one signature set-piece
29	  with at least two coordinated layers and a `?preview=` hook. **Motion always
30	  plays** (Anton, 2026-09-07 — FEEDBACK.md F-011, overrides the reduced-motion
31	  rule this replaced): never gate the reveal or the set-piece behind
32	  `prefers-reduced-motion` (F-011) or any other browser/OS accessibility
33	  setting, and never build a parallel static-fallback document. One motion path, verified
34	  once. This is a deliberate, permanent design-system override of the usual
35	  accessibility guidance — `a11y-audit` does not flag it. The set-piece's
36	  target (a window, a word, an object) is quiet at rest and lights on the
37	  first scroll: at rest the end state is never previewed. On a scroll brief,
38	  motion is the authority *inside* the set-piece act and type/photo step down
39	  there (TASTE.md § 4.8).
40	- **Two documented reveal profiles, not one.** The values above are the
41	  *editorial-print* reveal (28px, 1.2–1.4s) — a slow, deliberate arrival that
42	  suits a page whose sections are chapters. Scroll-craft's premium fade-in is
43	  the second profile and belongs to ordinary flow sections on a scroll page:
44	  **opacity from 0, a rise of about 14px over 620ms on an ease-out curve, 30–80ms
45	  stagger through the children in reading order, triggered slightly inside the
46	  viewport (`-12%` bottom root margin)** so it fires when the reader is looking
47	  rather than when the first pixel clears the fold. Its two failure bounds are
48	  exact and worth memorising: **a fade with no rise reads as a loading glitch; a
49	  rise past 24px reads as a slide.** *"Larger, slower, or bouncier is never more
50	  premium; the restraint is the signal."* **Conflict, resolved:** these are not
51	  competing values for the same thing — 28px/1.3s is the shared *page* reveal in
52	  the editorial registers, 14px/620ms is the *section* reveal on a scroll build,
53	  and a page picks one profile and holds it. What is never allowed is a third
54	  set of numbers invented per section, or a reveal that re-hides when the reader
55	  scrolls back up (that is a defect, not an effect).
56	- **A signature act may cost frames; the rest of the page may not.** Any
57	  continuous, CPU-heavy animation is isolated in a leaf element of its own so
58	  its work cannot invalidate the layout above it, and 60fps is the target, not
59	  the ambition (stitch § Motion: *"Isolated Client Components for CPU-heavy
60	  animations"*). Measurement, budget and the smoothness criteria live in
61	  `performance.md` and `motion-smoothness.md`.
62	- **Copy in a specific voice about a specific place**, with honest numbers.
63	- **Density above 7 puts every number in mono.** At dense settings the figures
64	  are the content, and proportional digits at that density read as noise —
65	  tabular mono is what makes a column of them scannable (stitch
66	  § High-density override). At the airy end of the scale this rule is off; a
67	  mono numeral in a 3-density editorial page is apparatus, and the apparatus
68	  budget in SKILL.md governs it instead.

70	### Craft vocabulary — the values that read as "made", not "generated"
71	
72	Small, specific, and the difference between a page that looks designed and one
73	that looks defaulted (designpowers `design-taste` § detail vocabulary):
74	
75	- **Borders are 1px at ~8 % opacity, not solid lines.** A solid rule at full
76	  strength is a divider from a template; a hairline at 8 % is a structure the
77	  eye reads without being interrupted by. Matches this file's *hairlines
78	  separate; planes do not*.
79	- **A shadow that must exist is two layers: one tight and sharp, one soft and
80	  ambient.** One layer reads as a sticker. **Conflict, noted:** the structural
81	  rule above still stands — depth is weight and scale first, `border` **or**
82	  `shadow` and never both (impeccable `craft-floor.md`), and
83	  `layout-and-space.md` § Depth bans stacked shadows *as a default*. The
84	  two-layer form is what a deliberate elevation looks like when the register has
85	  decided it needs one; it is not a licence to shadow every card.
86	- **Hover moves geometry, not colour** — `scale(1.02)`, a 1px lift, a rule
87	  drawing itself — rather than swapping a fill. A colour-swap hover is the
88	  cheapest and most generated-looking state on the page.
89	- **One radius vocabulary per page, spoken in roles**: e.g. 4px inputs, 8px
90	  cards, 16px modals. Three values with jobs, not seven values that happened.
91	  This is the Shape Consistency Lock (gate 92); the concentric-radius math in
92	  `layout-and-space.md` § Optical adjustments derives values *from* this
93	  vocabulary rather than adding to it.
94	- **The worked example of a coordinated two-layer set-piece** is
95	  `animated-navigation`: an arrow element flies from the logo to the hovered nav
96	  link while the link's underline expands from left to right — and the underline
97	  is held on `delay-300` so it starts *after* the arrow arrives. That delayed
98	  dependency is the whole lesson: two layers on one trigger, the second waiting
99	  on the first, so the motion reads as one gesture with a cause instead of two
100	  animations that happen to fire together. Its project values (the logo's
101	  arrow crop, the tuned coordinates, `/arrow.png`) are specific to that site and
102	  port nothing.

104	## Surviving the system's own overrides
105	
106	This house builds structure out of **hairlines, tone-on-tone planes and
107	low-opacity rules** (TASTE.md § 2.3). That is exactly the structure the
108	operating system throws away when a reader turns on a colour override — so the
109	page has to be built to survive it, not patched afterwards.
110	
111	- **`forced-colors: active` strips your colours and keeps your borders.**
112	  Windows High Contrast replaces every author colour with the system's own
113	  palette. A section boundary made of a 6 %-opacity rule, a `background`
114	  difference, or a tinted plane simply ceases to exist; the page collapses into
115	  one undifferentiated run. Don't fight the override — make sure **borders and
116	  outlines define every interactive element and every structural boundary**, and
117	  never let a background colour alone carry a state.
118	- **The transparent-border trick.** A `border: 1px solid transparent` is
119	  invisible in normal rendering and *becomes visible* under forced colours,
120	  because the system paints it. It is how a plane-and-hairline layout keeps its
121	  structure for free:
122	
123	  ```css
124	  .card, .section--ink, .ledger__row { border: 1px solid transparent; }
125	  ```
126	
127	  Then verify at `@media (forced-colors: active)` that every interactive element
128	  is still distinguishable (`inclusive/user-preference-respect` § forced-colors).
129	- **`prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce`** — outside F-011 entirely (it is a
130	  transparency preference, not a motion one), so honour it. It replaces
131	  semi-transparent surfaces with solid ones and removes frosted-glass and
132	  backdrop-blur effects; overlays
133	  become fully opaque. This costs this house almost nothing — glass is already
134	  refused (TASTE § 5, gate 60) and backdrop-blur is restricted to fixed/sticky
135	  chrome — but a scrim over a photograph does need a solid fallback, or the text
136	  above it loses its ground.
137	- **Motion is not in this list.** F-011: `prefers-reduced-motion` is not
138	  consulted, here or anywhere — motion always plays (see § Structural). Every
139	  *other* system preference in this section is honoured in full. The two are
140	  separate decisions and the override applies to exactly one of them.

142	## Editorial-print invariants — Calyx · Hōrai · Hyperborea only
143	
144	- **Kicker microformat** (identical across all three):
145	  `font-size: 10.5px; letter-spacing: 0.22em; text-transform: uppercase;`
146	  mono on Calyx/Hyperborea. The page's structural voice — labels, captions, meta.
147	- **Palette:** 8–10 named oklch tokens. Exactly ONE saturated accent, deployed
148	  at display scale (88px drop caps, clamp(3.8rem,7vw,6rem) prices, JP glyphs,
149	  the sun) and essentially never on small controls. A rare second accent
150	  (Hyperborea's crimson) is sparser still.
151	- **Buttons barely exist.** CTAs are typeset mailtos/links at italic text-4xl
152	  (Calyx line 274) or display-size headline links. Hyperborea's one button is a
153	  sharp amber rectangle.
154	- **Display type:** clamp() up to 15rem (Horai wordmark
155	  `clamp(4.5rem,15vw,15rem)`), leading 0.9–0.95, tracking ~-0.02em. Two-tone
156	  inside the headline: Calyx roman + italic Cardo in one line; Hyperborea
157	  cream + amber in one line. 2–3 families, hard roles. Body measure in ch
158	  (max-w-[36ch] … [58ch]).
159	- **Label-rail section anatomy:** 12-col grid, max-w 1480–1880px. col-span-3
160	  rail = kicker (accent or stone) + 1px rule at ~20% opacity + optional meta;
161	  col-span-9 content. Horai upgrades the rail with a JP glyph and
162	  `md:sticky md:top-32`.
163	- **Ledger, never card grid** — for pricing, indices, programmes, testimonials.
164	  Grid rows with hairline border-b at ~20% opacity, italic display numeral
165	  (`.01`, `I II III` at text-8xl), name + description capped at 44–54ch, meta
166	  in kicker, price right-aligned in display serif 3xl–8xl, currency in tiny
167	  kicker with Swedish thin-space formatting (`2 480 kr`).
168	- **Stagger:** paired photo/text columns offset `md:mt-24` / `md:mt-44`;
169	  programme columns `md:mt-12` / `md:mt-24`. Never top-aligned.
170	- **Grain film:** fixed full-page feTurbulence data-URI
171	  (`baseFrequency 0.85, numOctaves 2`) with feColorMatrix tinted to the
172	  palette; `mix-blend-mode: multiply` opacity .42–.5 on light ground,
173	  `screen` opacity .35 on dark. Those are the *editorial-print* values, where
174	  grain is a material choice carrying the printed-paper fiction. **On any other
175	  register grain has one job and one value: a flat dark ground bands on real
176	  displays, and grain at 4–5 % opacity is what makes it stop.** Scroll-craft
177	  states the effect exactly — it is *"the difference between 'a dark page' and
178	  'a lit room'"* (`taste.md` § Depth). Read 4–5 % as the functional floor for a
179	  dark build and .35–.5 as this register's deliberate excess; a cinematic or
180	  modern-clean page reaching for .42 has misread which of the two it is doing.
181	  Either way grain is a fixed, full-page, `pointer-events: none` layer.
182	- **Shared reveal:** `.reveal { opacity:0; transform:translateY(28px);
183	  transition: 1.2–1.4s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) }`, one IntersectionObserver
184	  at threshold 0.1–0.12; plays unconditionally, never neutralized by
185	  `prefers-reduced-motion` (F-011 motion-always override, 2026-09-07 —
186	  FEEDBACK.md). Reveals fail toward visible (threshold 0 for tall elements, mount
187	  reveal, failsafe, noscript — see the reveal guards).
188	- **One signature motion set-piece per page**, mathematically scrubbed, both
189	  directions, plus a `?preview=` debug hook forcing its formed state so it can
190	  be screenshot-verified.
191	- **Copy as worldbuilding:** commission numbers (`Cmsn. 0211 — Hotel Pigalle,
192	  Drottninggatan`), plate indices (`02 / 14`), edition markers (`Vol. IX ·
193	  spring`, `Edition MMXXVI · Vol. 03`), roman-numeral dates (`cut 14.iv`,
194	  `12.ix · friday`), real street addresses, cross-referenced fictional
195	  entities (Atelier Lichtspur is both the identity credit and a speaker's
196	  studio), self-aware colophons (`Set in Cardo & PT Mono`). Values encoded in
197	  copy: "120 seats. Three tiers. No platinum." / "Write us a letter, not a
198	  form."
199	- **In-situ negation:** section comments name the slop default replaced —
200	  "INDEX: a typeset price list / commission ledger — NOT a card row",
201	  "PROGRAMME: three-day numbered list (not 4 icon cards)".
202	- **Art direction by render:** photos judged under their actual scrims and
203	  swapped when they fought the type — "darker, moodier photo for the quote
204	  section (was bright meat plate which conflicted with overlay text)".

251	## Tidvatten — modern clean (cold-bath club, Malmö)
252	
253	Built blind by a subagent as a system test; the owner's read was that it felt the
254	least AI-generated of the set. Its lesson is that a grotesk can be a *decision*.
255	
256	- **Fonts:** Familjen Grotesk (display, uppercase, tight), Literata (body serif),
257	  Fragment Mono (kicker). The grotesk is right because the subject is temperature,
258	  timetable and protocol — precision, not connoisseurship.
259	- **Palette:** slate blue-greys and deep sea dark, terracotta as the only warmth,
260	  used exclusively at display scale.
261	- **Set-piece:** the two temperatures (`2°` / `85°`) driving together out of blur
262	  as the section centres — scrubbed both directions, with the mono line beneath
263	  resolving on a staged offset.
264	- **Anatomy:** full-bleed sea photograph with the wordmark set into it; a
265	  statutes ledger (`§4 · Tystnad på lavarna före klockan sju`); a numbered season
266	  programme; a staggered photo duo; a membership ledger.
267	- **Where it still slipped:** its values line was a translated clone of
268	  Hyperborea's. Hence the "borrow the move, never the sentence" rule.

270	## Klova — warm photographic (harbour restaurant, Bohuslän)
271	
272	The counter-example that proves the register split. It breaks nearly every
273	editorial invariant and is correct. Full notes in `sites/klova/README.md`.
274	
275	- **Centred logo lockup over a full-bleed photograph.** No rail, no kicker, no
276	  edition marker.
277	- **A real outlined button** (`SE VÅR MENY`), sized to be pressed. A typeset
278	  mailto at text-4xl would be affectation here.
279	- **Rounded corners, generous air** around images; a dotted carousel for the food
280	  gallery. Both patterns the editorial registers reject, both right here.
281	- **No grain, no apparatus, no colophon, no ledger.** The menu is a menu.
282	- **Warm serif display at conversational size** over a plain sans body. The
283	  headline welcomes rather than announces.
284	- **Dark navy footer** as the tonal inversion — the one structural invariant it
285	  keeps unchanged.

287	## How to use this file
288	
289	**Pick the register from the business first**, then match that register's
290	inventory plus the structural section — never the pixels, and never another
291	register's apparatus. A new build shares the structure (one display-scale accent,
292	hierarchy through scale, hairlines, stagger, weighted columns, one set-piece)
293	while its palette, faces, apparatus policy and world are its own.
294	
295	If a section is about to become a card grid, a rounded gradient pill, or three
296	same-rhythm text blocks, this file is the list of what to do instead. If a page is
297	about to receive its eighth 10px mono caption, the answer is in the apparatus
298	budget in SKILL.md, not here.

Otherwise skip it, or use one functional line. 102 103 --- 104 105 ## Copy tells 106 107 ### 84 · Performative-craftsman labels and social proof 108 - `Quietly in use at` / `Quietly trusted by` → use `Trusted by`, `Used at`, or let the logos speak. 109 - `From the field` / `Field notes` / `Currently on the bench` / `On our desks` / `Loose plates` → use plain functional labels (`Testimonials`, `Latest writing`) or none. 110 - Mock-humble industry asides (`We respect the French ones`). 111 112 Partially mechanical: impeccable's `theater-slop-phrase` and `marketing-buzzword` catch some phrasings. 113 114 ### 85 · Atmospheric locale, time, and weather strips 115 `LIS 14:23 · 18°C` in a nav, `Lisbon, working with founders` in a hero, `1200-690 Lisbon, Portugal` as a footer flourish. Allowed only for a genuinely timezone-distributed studio, a travel brand, or a real physical venue. A plain contact address in the footer is fine; an atmospheric strip is not. 116 117 --- 118 119 ## Lists and comparison visuals 120 121 ### 86 · `border-t` + `border-b` on every row 122 A ten-row spec table with a hairline under each row is the laziest available layout. Pick one (bottom border between rows, or a top border above the group) and use it sparingly. For lists over five items, reach for a real UI component instead of `
    ` + `divide-y`. 123 124 ### 87 · Scoring bars with filled background tracks 125 `bg-zinc-200` tracks with a partial fill, used as a comparison visual on a marketing page. Dashboard clutter. Prefer a number plus a small icon, or a thin inline bar with no background track. 126 127 --- 128 129 ## Scroll cues 130 131 ### 88 · Any scroll cue 132 `Scroll`, `↓ scroll`, `Scroll to explore`, `Scroll to walk through it`, animated mouse-wheel icons. If the visitor has not scrolled, they are looking at the hero — they know what scrolling is. The bottom of the viewport does not need a label. 133 134 --- 135 136 ## Chrome that appears whatever the subject 137 138 ### 97 · `→` appended to link and button text 139 140 `Book a meeting →`, `Read more →`, `Get started →`, `Se caset →`. Upstream names it in 141 the same breath as the tracked-out eyebrow and the middle-dot meta string: *"template 142 chrome that appears whatever the subject … a '→' appended to link and button text"* 143 (`upstream/anthropic/frontend-design/SKILL.md`). The arrow is not the direction of 144 anything on the page; it is decoration that means *this is a link*, applied to text that 145 already is one. 146 147 Banned as default, on links, buttons, cards-as-links, nav items and CTA rows alike. The 148 arrow is permitted only when [`reference-lock.md`](reference-lock.md)'s decision ledger 149 carries a row for it — a named source that does it, and a reason specific to this brief. 150 Absent that row, the affordance is carried by a typeset underline, a real button, or the 151 label's own verb. 152 153 **[ours]** This is a sibling of gate 73 (middle dot as default joiner) and gate 84 154 (performative labels): each one is a small mark the model adds to signal craft. Two CTAs 155 on the same page both ending in `→` is the shape to look for first, because it proves the 156 arrow is a habit and not a decision. 157 158 ### 98 · Dark ground with no `color-scheme` and no `theme-color` 159 160 A page whose canvas is dark (cinematic dark, illustrated dark, or any locked dark theme) 161 that never declares it to the browser. Refero states the consequence plainly: *"Without 162 `color-scheme: dark`, scrollbars stay light gray on dark backgrounds"*, form controls 163 `` / `

1	# Gates
2	
3	**Load on every build.** Numbered, citable, non-negotiable. A hook that denies a write cites a gate number; so should you when you waive one.
4	
5	Three sources, one numbering space:
6	
7	| Range | Source | Where the detail lives |
8	|---|---|---|
9	| **1–57** | Hallmark slop-test | [`slop-test.md`](slop-test.md) — ported verbatim, **source of truth** |
10	| **58–65** | This repo — the gate order, scope, and derivation rules | Below |
11	| **66–88** | `design-taste-frontend` v2 production-test tells | [`production-tells.md`](production-tells.md) — micro-decoration signatures |
12	| **89–91** | This repo — reference-lock discipline (Refero-derived) | Below |
13	| **92–96** | This repo — shape, budget, continuity, provenance, profile | Below |
14	| **97–98** | `design-taste-frontend` v2, ported 2026-09-09 — two further production tells | [`production-tells.md`](production-tells.md) |
15	| **mechanical** | impeccable v4 detector, 68 deterministic rules | `detect.mjs`, mapped below |
16	
17	The numbering space is shared and append-only: 66–88 and 97–98 both live in
18	`production-tells.md`, and a new tell takes the next free number rather than
19	extending 88, because 89–96 are already spent here.
20	
21	Do not restate 1–57 here. Read [`slop-test.md`](slop-test.md). Do not restate 66–88 or 97–98 here. Read [`production-tells.md`](production-tells.md).
22	
23	**Why 66–88 exist separately.** Gates 1–57 catch structural and visual slop. Gates 66–88 catch *micro-decoration* — version labels, numbered eyebrows, middle-dot chains, status dots, photo-credit captions, scroll cues, locale strips. Each looks like a deliberate designer choice in isolation; together they are the most recognisable AI-page signature in production. Load them on every marketing, landing, or portfolio build.
24	
25	---
26	
27	## Both directions — the rule that governs every gate here
28	
29	> **Every load-bearing check is proved in BOTH directions: a fixture that must fall, and
30	> a known-good build that must stay silent. A check that can only fire is as worthless
31	> as one that never does.**
32	
33	A gate nobody has watched fire is an assumption. A gate that has never been held against
34	a build you already trust is worse — it will fire on that build too, and the first time
35	it does, someone waives it, and from then on the gate is decoration.
36	
37	So each numbered gate, each hook denial and each script threshold needs two proofs on
38	file:
39	
40	| Direction | What it proves | Where the fixtures live |
41	|---|---|---|
42	| **Must fall** | The detection actually detects | `tests/fixtures/`, `tests/a11y/broken.html`, `tests/perf/heavy.html`, `tests/motion/staircase.html` |
43	| **Must stay silent** | The threshold is not over-greedy | a catalogue entry, `sites/calyx.html`, `tests/perf/clean.html`, `tests/motion/smooth.html` |
44	
45	**A check that flags the reference build is too greedy and gets narrowed — never
46	waived.** `blankBands` in `scroll_verify.py` is exactly such a check: it can fire on the
47	deliberately quiet act before the peak that `scroll/feel-and-fingerprint.md` requires. The
48	fix is a narrower band definition, not an exception for that page. Waiving is for a
49	*brief* that overrides a gate (see § Waiving a gate); it is never the answer to a gate
50	that misfires.
51	
52	This is why `verify-design-system.py` runs paired fixtures rather than asserting on
53	output text, and why a new gate is not finished when its rule is written — it is finished
54	when both fixtures exist.
55	
56	---
57	
58	## Gates 58–65 · the gate-order rules
59	
60	These exist because Tiers 0–2 are this system's contribution and nothing upstream enforces them.
61	
62	### 58 · Tier not declared
63	
64	Did the build state its tier out loud before picking any token? If no tier was named, fail. Silent tier selection is how Tier 1 gets skipped — the model reads brand evidence, does not register it as authority, and invents anyway. The declaration is cheap and makes the omission visible: *"Tier 1 — deriving from the Snajp wordmark and the existing type scale."*
65	
66	### 59 · Token not traceable to tier evidence
67	
68	At Tiers 0–2, can every colour, face, radius, and spacing step be traced to a named source — a `DESIGN.md` entry, a file in the codebase, the logo, the studied reference? A token that cannot be traced was invented, and invention is Tier 3 only. Fail per untraceable token. At Tier 3 this gate passes trivially.
69	
70	### 60 · Demoted-skill palette in a Tier 0–2 build
71	
72	Does the output contain a hardcoded value from a skill whose palette is fixed?
73	
74	| Skill | Values that trip this gate |
75	|---|---|
76	| `minimalist-ui` | `#F7F6F3` `#FBFBFA` `#F9F9F8` `#EAEAEA` `#111111` `#2F3437` `#787774` `#333333` `#FDEBEC` `#E1F3FE` `#EDF3EC` `#FBF3DB` `#9F2F2D` `#1F6C9F` `#346538` `#956400` |
77	| `industrial-brutalist-ui` | `#F4F4F0` `#EAE8E3` `#050505` `#0A0A0A` `#121212` `#E61919` `#FF2A2A` `#4AF626` |
78	| `high-end-visual-design` | `#050505` `#FDFBF7` |
79	
80	Auto-fail at Tiers 0–2. These skills may contribute craft vocabulary — spacing rhythm, detail patterns, elevation logic — but their palettes are overridden by the locked tokens. At Tier 3 the gate passes if the skill was chosen deliberately and by name.
81	
82	**This gate is the instrumented trap.** Every firing is logged to the session ledger as a `trap` event with the file and whether it was caught before or after the write. See [`component-routing.md`](component-routing.md) § Telemetry.
83	
84	### 61 · Undefined link colours
85	
86	Are default `a` and `a:hover` colours defined from the palette, even when the page currently has no links? If not, fail. Links added later render browser-default blue, which is off-brand on every design ever made.
87	
88	### 62 · Mobile hit target below 44px
89	
90	Does every interactive element present at least a 44×44px touch target at mobile widths? Padding counts; visual size does not have to change. Fail per element below the floor.
91	
92	### 63 · Value snapped to a framework default
93	
94	Was a source value rounded to a grid step or a framework token? `13px` must not become `14px`; `5px` must not become `4px`; a brand orange must not become the nearest Tailwind orange. The source is ground truth and its odd numbers are the brand. Fail per snapped value.
95	
96	Mechanically covered by `design-system-radius`, `design-system-font-size`, and `design-system-color` once `DESIGN.md` exists.
97	
98	### 64 · Change beyond the ask
99	
100	On a targeted request, did anything change besides what was asked? Layout, spacing, margins, fonts, sizes, positions, colours, and content outside the named target must be byte-identical. Improvements are *suggested in the reply*, never applied. Fail on any unrequested diff hunk.
101	
102	Does not apply to redesign, new direction, or from-scratch requests — those are substantial by definition. See [`scope-discipline.md`](scope-discipline.md).
103	
104	### 65 · Second identity inside an established surface
105	
106	Does a new section, component, feature, or state introduce type, colour, motion, or component language that does not exist elsewhere on the surface? A local addition inherits; it does not start a second identity. Check the eight axes in [`scope-discipline.md`](scope-discipline.md) § inheritance checklist. Fail on any axis that diverges without the user asking for it.
107	
108	---
109	
110	## Gates 89–91 · reference-lock and averaging
111	
112	These exist because [`reference-lock.md`](reference-lock.md) is this repo's
113	contribution and nothing upstream enforces it. Each fires whether the build
114	skipped the lock entirely or filled it out and drifted from it anyway.
115	
116	### 89 · Calm-editorial autopilot
117	
118	**Rule.** Warm ivory + oversized serif + one italic/serif word swap +
119	olive/clay/terracotta, applied without a register that earns it, fails. Licensed
120	only in the **editorial-print register** when the business plausibly publishes an
121	edition, catalogue, or archive — and even there, never the same word-swap two
122	generations running.
123	**Detection.** Palette traces {olive, clay, terracotta} + serif display + one
124	word carrying italic/serif/colour contrast, on a business with no editorial-print
125	justification, or the identical word-swap recurring from the prior generation.
126	**Fix.** Re-run Step 2 honestly — derive the register from the business, not from
127	taste. See [`reference-lock.md`](reference-lock.md) § Anti-averaging and the
128	identity / editorial litmus tests.
129	
130	### 90 · Reference averaging
131	
132	**Rule.** A build whose palette, type, or structure sits at the safe
133	intersection of conflicting references — instead of committing to one dominant
134	direction — fails, per **dark + acid + serif ≠ cream + orange + polite serif**.
135	**Detection.** Compare the built tokens against each captured reference in the
136	decision ledger; if no single reference dominates and the result reads as a
137	softened middle of all of them, it's averaged.
138	**Fix.** Name one primary reference and rebuild the lock's "Preserve" and
139	"Borrow only" fields around it. See [`reference-lock.md`](reference-lock.md) §
140	Anti-averaging.
141	
142	### 91 · Token-role drift
143	
144	**Rule.** A token or component pulled from a source reference keeps the role
145	that source gave it — a CTA-only accent used as a background, a code-only colour
146	used as UI chrome, or a decorative gradient promoted to a core surface all fail.
147	**Detection.** Walk the reference-lock's "Role rules" field against the built
148	page; flag every token or component whose deployed role doesn't match its
149	declared one.
150	**Fix.** Restore the token to its licensed role or drop it — never repurpose it
151	to make a layout "work." See [`reference-lock.md`](reference-lock.md) §
152	Token-role and media-role preservation.
153	
154	---
155	
156	## Gates 92–96 · shape, budget, continuity, provenance, profile
157	
158	Five checks that existed as prose in five different files and could not be cited by a
159	hook, a reviewer or a waiver. Each has a mechanical detection and each is proved in both
160	directions per the rule at the top of this file.
161	
162	### 92 · Shape Consistency Lock
163	
164	**Rule.** One radius scale per page — sharp (0), one mid step (12–16), or pill — or a
165	written rule saying which element class gets which. Mixing 4, 8, 12, 16, 24 and pill
166	across one surface with no rule behind it fails. The failure has a signature and it is
167	**8 px on everything**: TASTE.md § 2.5, counted across the 89 sources Anton actually
168	saved, says rounding is a decision — either 0–3 px or large and deliberate (Raus 20/40,
169	Bumble 16–24, pill 999) — and *"Ingen ligger på 8 px-default."*
170	**Detection.** Collect every `border-radius` value in the emitted CSS. More than one
171	radius family, with no rule for it in `DESIGN.md` or `BRIEF.md`, fails.
172	`design-system-radius` covers this mechanically **once `DESIGN.md` exists**; this gate is
173	what holds before it does, which on a single-file HTML page is always. A reference's
174	radius vocabulary (`design-taste`'s 4 / 8 / 16) is a set to pick *from*, not a licence to
175	use all of it.
176	**Fix.** Name the scale in the token block (`--radius-sm` / `--radius-lg` /
177	`--radius-pill`), derive it from the locked reference, and restate every exception as a
178	rule rather than as a loose value. Gate **63** still binds on top: a source radius of
179	14 px stays 14 px and does not snap to 16.
180	
181	### 93 · Performance budget
182	
183	**Rule.** A page ships only when every line of [`performance.md`](performance.md) § 1 has
184	been **measured on this page** and met. A number nobody measured is a failed row, not a
185	pass — the same failure as an invented metric in copy (gate **46**).
186	**Detection.** `scripts/perf_probe.py` served through `scripts/serve.py`, at `--cpu 4`,
187	at 1440×900 and 390×844. Fail per row over its limit: LCP ≤ 1.8 s · CLS ≤ 0.05 · zero
188	long tasks during scroll · frame p95 ≤ 20 ms with none over 33 ms · ≤ 2.5 MB transferred
189	at 1440 · hero ≤ 250 kB WebP · ≤ 3 font files / 300 kB · ≤ 1500 DOM nodes · zero resting
190	`will-change` · no `filter`/`backdrop-filter` over half the viewport. A scrubbed clip has
191	its own line (≤ 32 MiB desktop, ≤ 16 MiB mobile, fetched as a Blob after first paint) and
192	does not count against the page. Never measure through `python -m http.server`: it is
193	HTTP/1.0 and drops large WebP responses under Chromium on Windows, so the run measures a
194	page that failed to load.
195	**Fix.** [`performance.md`](performance.md) §§ 2–3 in order, loading before rendering.
196	Two of the rows are structural rather than numeric and are fixed by deletion: a hero on
197	another company's CDN, and `will-change` set on a class.
198	
199	### 94 · Motion continuity
200	
201	**Rule.** Anything the eye sees move is damped, evenly paced, and holds frame. Three
202	parts, and they fail independently:
203	
204	1. **Damped.** Bespoke motion reads `--sc-ps`, never raw `--sc-p`, whenever it drives
205	   `transform`, `object-position`, `clip-path`, `mask-position` or `background-position`.
206	   Cue opacity may read `--sc-p`.
207	2. **Continuous.** At 4× CPU throttling, in **both** scroll directions: `staircase` 0,
208	   `frame_p95_ms` ≤ 20, `frames_over_33ms` 0, and `max_step_pct` ≤ 3 **on the damped
209	   playhead (`--sc-ps`)**. On a derived track (`transform`, `clip-path`, …) `max_step` is
210	   reported, not gated: a smoothstepped value peaks at ~4.4 % per frame by its own
211	   derivative, and `staircase` already catches the step. (r8 R2, 2026-09-09: V3c's flip
212	   read 4.12 % with staircase 0 and was correct.) Never track raw `--sc-p` — it steps
213	   per wheel tick by design.
214	3. **Evenly paced.** On a multi-act or multi-leg sequence, `rate = weight / clip_seconds`
215	   holds within ~6 % across the whole run. 36 % is the measured failure, not a
216	   hypothetical one — see [`scroll/pace.md`](scroll/pace.md).
217	
218	**Detection.** `scripts/motion_probe.py --track "<sel>:<prop>,…" --cpu 4` over every
219	value the eye sees move; the script enforces those four thresholds itself. Grep the
220	emitted source for `--sc-p` inside a `transform` / `clip-path` / `object-position` /
221	`mask-position` / `background-position` declaration. Per-leg rates are arithmetic off the
222	markup — weight and clip length are both in the source, so there is no excuse for not
223	having the table.
224	**Fix.** Diagnose which fault you have *before* changing anything
225	([`motion-smoothness.md`](motion-smoothness.md) § The two faults): damp the value, or cut
226	the work (gate **93**). They need opposite fixes, and an afternoon spent smoothing
227	something that was never stepping is the standard way to lose one.
228	
229	### 95 · Catalogue selection not logged
230	
231	**Rule.** The references were chosen mechanically out of the whole catalogue, and the
232	`catalogue-select` row in `.impeccable/design-session.jsonl` is the proof. References
233	recalled from memory, or handed down in an orchestrator's prompt, fail — **even when they
234	are the right ones.** r7 named the right slugs, the builders read them, the reference
235	floor was satisfied, and `Skill(design-catalog)` was never invoked; nothing afterwards
236	could tell the difference. This gate is that difference.
237	**Detection.** The ledger carries a `catalogue-select` row naming **≥ 2 slugs**; every
238	named slug has its `entry.md` and a fold read in the same session, plus its
239	`extract/*-DESIGN.md` where an extract exists; on a scroll brief
240	`design-fingerprints.md` was read as well. `hooks/design-gate.py`'s reference floor denies
241	the first UI write until those marks are present.
242	**Fix.** `python scripts/catalogue/select.py --brief BRIEF.md --k 4 --wildcard --explain`,
243	then read what comes back as pixels *and* as text and rewrite the lock from it. An empty
244	result means widen the register, drop the grammar, or try an adjacent category — it is
245	not permission to work from memory. See [`catalogue-first.md`](catalogue-first.md) § 5.
246	
247	### 96 · TASTE § 5 hit
248	
249	**Rule.** TASTE.md § 5 is the rejected list, derived by counting occurrences across the 89
250	sources Anton actually saved rather than from taste: *"Ett bygge som innehåller något ur
251	listan ovan ligger utanför profilen oavsett hur välgjort det är."* A nonzero count is not
252	a licence — it names the single licensed form (Palais' blobs are hand-drawn;
253	dope.security's indigo is a glow, not an accent). The gate fires on the generic form.
254	**Detection.** Ten items, mapped to what actually checks them:
255	
256	| TASTE § 5 item | In 89 saved sources | Mechanical rule |
257	|---|---|---|
258	| Icon grid | 0 | `icon-tile-stack` |
259	| Gradient mesh | 1 (Brand Federation, saved for the hero shape) | none exact; nearest `radial-halo`, `radial-spotlight-glow`, `repeating-stripes-gradient`. **By eye** |
260	| Glassmorphism | 0 | none. **By eye** |
261	| Centred hero with a badge row | 0 (outside AI templates) | `hero-eyebrow-chip` catches the badge; the centring is a critique measurement (taste-skill § 4.3, anti-centre above variance 4), not a detector rule |
262	| Purple / indigo accent | 1 (dope.security, as a glow) | `ai-color-palette`, plus the flat-accent hexes `#6366f1` `#8b5cf6` `#7c3aed` in [`color.md`](color.md) § Bans |
263	| Shadowed 8 px cards | 3 (all template defaults) | `gpt-thin-border-wide-shadow`, `border-accent-on-rounded` — and gate **92** |
264	| Stock photo of a smiling team | 0 | none. **By eye** |
265	| "h1 48 / h2 32" scale | 0 | `flat-type-hierarchy` (`oversized-h1` is the opposite failure) |
266	| Decorative blobs | 1 (Palais, hand-drawn) | `shape-assembled-illustration` |
267	| Three identical feature cards | 4 (all in AI templates) | `repeated-container-text` |
268	
269	**Fix.** Replace the move; never soften it into a version that scores under the
270	threshold. Four of the ten have no mechanical rule and are read by eye at Step 5 pass 10
271	([`verbs/critique.md`](verbs/critique.md)) — that is a known coverage gap, written down
272	here rather than papered over.
273	
274	---
275	
276	## Reinterpreting gate 57
277	
278	`slop-test.md` gate 57 fires when a `study` diagnosis is discarded in favour of a catalog theme. Its principle generalises to our gate order and is read as: **any derived or studied system discarded for a catalog theme, at any tier above 3, is an auto-fail.** The specific catalog-theme name list in the ported text is the Tier-3 vocabulary; the failure it describes — reverting to the attractor after doing the derivation work — is exactly what gates 59 and 60 catch at Tiers 1 and 2.
279	
280	The ported file is not edited. This paragraph is the reinterpretation.
281	
282	---
283	
284	## Mechanical coverage
285	
286	`detect.mjs` carries 68 deterministic rules. Run it once over changed files at Step 5; parse the JSON, because **exit code stays 0 when findings exist**.
287	
288	```bash
289	node "$HOME/.agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/detect.mjs" --json <files>
290	```
291	
292	Contract rules — these read `DESIGN.md` directly and are what `design-gate.py` denies on:
293	
294	| Rule id | Enforces |
295	|---|---|
296	| `design-system-color` | Colour outside the `DESIGN.md` palette |
297	| `design-system-font` | Face not declared in `DESIGN.md` typography |
298	| `design-system-font-size` | Size outside the declared scale |
299	| `design-system-radius` | Radius outside the declared scale |
300	
301	Slop rules overlapping our numbered gates: `side-tab` (gate 3 family), `gradient-text`, `dark-glow`, `radial-halo`, `radial-spotlight-glow`, `overused-font`, `italic-serif-display` (38a), `nested-cards`, `icon-tile-stack`, `hero-eyebrow-chip`, `numbered-section-labels` (54 family), `repeated-section-kickers`, `oversized-h1`, `flat-type-hierarchy`, `cream-palette`, `ai-color-palette`, `border-accent-on-rounded`, `gpt-thin-border-wide-shadow`, `edge-flush-cards`, `repeating-stripes-gradient`, `shape-assembled-illustration`, `codex-grid-background`.
302	
303	Layout and responsive: `clipped-overflow-container`, `text-overflow`, `text-occlusion`, `first-viewport-column-overflow`, `body-text-viewport-edge`, `broken-image`, `image-hover-transform`, `layout-transition`.
304	
305	Type and legibility: `low-contrast`, `gray-on-color`, `tiny-text`, `undersized-ui-text`, `line-length`, `tight-leading`, `wide-tracking`, `extreme-negative-tracking`, `all-caps-body`, `justified-text`, `single-font`, `heading-rhythm`, `skipped-heading`.
306	
307	Copy — these run before the copy gate and catch its cheapest cases mechanically: `em-dash-overuse`, `marketing-buzzword`, `theater-slop-phrase`, `aphoristic-cadence`, `repeated-container-text`.
308	
309	Motion and state: `bounce-easing`, `blinking-cursor`, `pulsing-dot`, `marquee`, `content-hidden-at-rest`, `monotonous-spacing`, `cramped-padding`, `script-error`.
310	
311	**Not mechanically covered** — gates 58, 59, 60, 64, 65 and the whole gate order are model-enforced. `design-gate.py` and `design-route.py` cover 60 and 63 by pattern; the rest are judgment and are why the pre-emit self-critique exists.
312	
313	Of the new block: **93** and **94** are fully mechanical (`perf_probe.py`, `motion_probe.py` — both already enforce their own thresholds), **95** is enforced by `design-gate.py`'s reference floor, **92** is mechanical only once `DESIGN.md` exists (`design-system-radius`) and model-enforced before that, and **96** is mechanical for six of its ten items — the four marked *by eye* in its table are the coverage gap.
314	
315	---
316	
317	## Waiving a gate
318	
319	A gate may be waived only when the user's own brief calls for it. Say which gate, and why the brief overrides it, in one line. Never waive silently, and never waive by softening the element — rewrite it or keep it.
320	
321	impeccable v4's rule governs: **the brief wins; your own habit does not.**
322	
323	Persistent, project-wide exceptions go through the detector's config rather than being re-argued each session:
324	
325	```bash
326	node "$HOME/.agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/hook-admin.mjs" ignore-value overused-font <Font> --shared --reason "..."

1	# `design critique`
2	
3	Visual critique: the positive quality gate, judged on pixels.
4	
5	Audit (`verbs/audit.md`) catches slop — named anti-patterns, structural
6	templates, gate violations. Critique is the other half: does this page read as
7	*good*, independent of whether it committed a named sin. A page can pass every
8	gate and still be flat, timid, or off-brand. Critique is where that gets
9	caught. Ported from [`upstream/designer-skills/visual-critique/`](../upstream/designer-skills/visual-critique/)
10	(seven `critique-*` skills + `/critique-screen`), adapted to this system's
11	tokens and register model in place of generic UI screens.
12	
13	**Contract**
14	- **Reads:** the screenshots actually captured (fold, full page in slices,
15	  mobile 390) — `Read` each PNG so it enters context, never judge from code or
16	  memory. `DESIGN.md` if locked, or the tier-2 study notes / register table in
17	  [`house-physics.md`](../house-physics.md). The named references from Step 1b.
18	- **Does:** scores seven dimensions against what is on screen, each rated
19	  `pass` / `minor` / `major`, and runs the squint test and the composition
20	  contract.
21	- **Writes:** nothing. Critique is judgment, not code. Output is the fix list
22	  below, handed to a build or polish pass.
23	- **Human checks:** the assessment paragraph and the honest reference
24	  comparison are claims a reviewer should be able to verify by looking at the
25	  same screenshots — cite what you saw, not what a good page usually has.
26	
27	---
28	
29	## A/B isolation — how this verb is run
30	
31	Ported from impeccable `critique.md` § Hard Invariants. The seven dimensions
32	below are one of two assessments, not the whole verb.
33	
34	- **Assessment A — design review.** The dimensions, the squint test, the
35	  composition contract, the personas. Judged on the read images.
36	- **Assessment B — detector and browser evidence.**
37	  `node ~/.agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/detect.mjs --json <target>` plus
38	  what the rendered page actually reports (console errors, failed requests).
39	
40	**Both are required, and they run as two isolated sub-agents whenever a Task
41	tool exists.** *"Running them inline in this context is 'possible' but is NOT
42	permitted; it is a degraded run."* The reason is stated in the same file and it
43	is the point of the whole arrangement: *"Assessment A must finish before
44	detector findings enter the parent synthesis context. Detector output is
45	deterministic, but it still anchors judgment."* A critic who has already read a
46	list of 14 mechanical findings will write a critique shaped by that list.
47	
48	**The banner is not optional.** If A and B ran in one context for any reason,
49	the report's first line is:
50	
51	```text
52	⚠️ DEGRADED: single-context (<reason>)
53	```
54	
55	*"A silent degraded critique is a failed critique."* A dual-agent run declares
56	itself the same way: `Method: dual-agent (A: <agent-id> · B: <agent-id>)`.
57	A skipped detector is a failed run unless `detect.mjs` is missing or crashes
58	after a real attempt.
59	
60	**Synthesis is weaving, not concatenation.** Say where the read and the detector
61	agree, where the detector caught what the read missed, and where a detector
62	finding is a false positive in this context.
63	
64	---
65	
66	## Inputs
67	
68	Before scoring anything, confirm you actually have:
69	
70	1. **The screenshots that were read** — fold (first viewport), full page in
71	   slices, and mobile at 390px. A dimension scored from source code instead of
72	   a captured, read image is not a visual critique; say so and mark it
73	   `not verified` rather than guessing from CSS.
74	2. **The direction document** — `DESIGN.md` if the project is Tier 0/locked,
75	   otherwise the lane phrase and register named in Step 1b/Step 2 of
76	   [`../../SKILL.md`](../../SKILL.md) (e.g. *"Tier 1 — warm photographic,
77	   deriving from the harbour-restaurant brand"*). This stands in for
78	   upstream's `mood.md`/`voice.md` — this system does not maintain those
79	   files. If neither exists, brand consistency is scored `N/A`, not invented.
80	3. **House physics** — [`house-physics.md`](../house-physics.md), the
81	   register's inventory, for what "good" looks like in this specific lane.
82	
83	---
84	
85	## The seven dimensions
86	
87	Run in this order. For each: **Observation** (neutral, what is actually on
88	screen) → **Problem** (what is broken and why it matters) → **Fix** (specific,
89	actionable). Rate `pass` / `minor` / `major`.
90	
91	### 1 · Hierarchy
92	- **Entry point** — one dominant element; does it match the primary goal?
93	- **Eye flow** — deliberate path (F/Z/register-appropriate), no dead ends.
94	- **Weight** — size differential ≥1.5× between adjacent hierarchy levels.
95	- **Emphasis** — exactly one primary emphasis zone; is it earned?
96	
97	### 2 · Composition
98	- **Balance** — visual weight distributed on purpose, not by accident. Is the
99	  composition symmetrically or asymmetrically balanced, and *is the choice
100	  intentional*? Are heavy elements (dark fills, large images, dense text)
101	  offset by lighter ones? Does the layout tip — top-heavy, bottom-heavy,
102	  left-leaning? Is there a clear visual centre of gravity?
103	- **Whitespace** — macro air between sections, consistent micro-spacing. Does
104	  the whitespace *guide* attention, or does it fragment the layout into
105	  disconnected areas?
106	- **Rhythm** — spacing intervals off a scale; repeated elements uniform.
107	  Variety without chaos: a balance of repetition and differentiation, with
108	  section breaks that create a legible page cadence.
109	- **Gestalt** — proximity, similarity, figure/ground, continuity, closure.
110	  Related elements close together *and* unrelated ones clearly separated;
111	  elements that share a function share a treatment; alignment and flow lines
112	  lead the eye through the composition.
113	- **Anti-centre** — at a declared variance above 4 (the BRIEF.md dial), a
114	  centred hero or centred H1 section is a finding, not a preference. The
115	  alternatives upstream names are split-screen 50/50, left-aligned content with
116	  a right-aligned asset, asymmetric whitespace, or a scroll-pinned structure.
117	  Override: *"centered hero is OK for editorial / manifesto /
118	  launch-announcement briefs where the message itself is the design"* — which
119	  is the same carve-out gate 6's genre note already makes. This is the
120	  measurable form of "never converge": count the centred axes, don't intuit
121	  them.
122	- **Cohesion** — *"the overall composition feels cohesive — like one designer,
123	  not a committee."* Scan the full-page slices for the giveaway: three sections
124	  that each look like a competent solution to their own problem and share no
125	  spacing rhythm, no rule weight, no heading pattern.
126	
127	### 3 · Typography
128	- **Scale usage** — only defined steps; each step used for its role.
129	- **Readability** — measure capped 45–75ch; line-height by role (headings
130	  ~1.1, body 1.4–1.6, anything wrapping 3+ lines ≥1.4); contrast AA.
131	- **Consistency** — semantically equal elements share one treatment.
132	- **Token compliance** — every size/weight/family traces to a token, never a
133	  raw value improvised mid-render (gate 48, gate 59).
134	
135	### 4 · Colour
136	- **Measured contrast pairs** — the rendered foreground against the ground it
137	  actually sits on, not the page background; state the ratio and the
138	  threshold it missed. Never report a ratio you didn't measure.
139	- **Palette coherence** — limited to the locked tokens; the one saturated
140	  accent stays at display scale, never fill on a small control.
141	- **Semantic use** — state never carried by colour alone; status hues
142	  consistent; interactive colour distinguishable from decorative.
143	- **CVD / forced-colours** — holds up for deuteranopia/protanopia and in a
144	  forced-colours environment.
145	
146	### 5 · Affordance
147	- **Clickability** — controls read as controls; no false or missing
148	  affordances; hit area ≥44×44px on mobile (gate 62).
149	- **States** — default/hover/focus-visible/active/disabled/loading present
150	  and distinct; focus ring visible against its ground.
151	- **Single CTA** — one dominant action per view; primary filled, secondary
152	  ghost/outline, never two filled CTAs competing.
153	- **Discoverability** — nothing load-bearing hidden behind hover-only on a
154	  touch surface; empty states name a next action.
155	
156	### 6 · Information density
157	- **Cognitive load** — how many decisions to complete the primary task; is
158	  anything present that doesn't serve it. Score the eight-item checklist below.
159	- **One primary action** — *"One primary action per screen. If everything is
160	  important, nothing is."* (designpowers `cognitive-accessibility`.) A view with
161	  two equally weighted primary actions has not decided what it is for.
162	- **No hostile timing** — *"timed actions are hostile."* A countdown, an
163	  auto-advancing carousel that moves the thing being read, a session that
164	  expires mid-form: if a timeout is genuinely necessary, it warns before it
165	  expires and allows extension.
166	- **Input is preserved** — *"if a form submission fails, do not clear the
167	  fields."* Clearing a form on error is the single most expensive small defect
168	  a page can carry, because it converts one mistake into abandonment.
169	- **Priority** — the thing the user needs is above the fold and visually
170	  dominant; nothing critical buried in low-contrast secondary text.
171	- **Scanning pattern** — layout matches how it's actually read; labels
172	  aligned; numbers/dates formatted consistently.
173	- **Progressive disclosure** — complexity deferred where it should be,
174	  primary actions never hidden behind a disclosure to achieve this.
175	
176	### 7 · Brand consistency
177	Compare against `DESIGN.md` if locked, or the named lane/register sentence
178	and house-physics inventory otherwise. **Never invent a `mood.md` or
179	`voice.md` to check against — if the project has neither a `DESIGN.md` nor a
180	stated lane, mark this dimension `N/A` and say why**, rather than inventing
181	brand rules that don't exist in this system.
182	- **Mood/register** — does the visual language match the named lane and the
183	  register table's fit (editorial print / cinematic dark / illustrated dark /
184	  modern clean / warm photographic / historical art)?
185	- **Voice** — does visible copy match the tone the lane implies; any
186	  off-register apparatus (kicker microformat, grain, ledgers) borrowed from a
187	  register this page isn't in?
188	- **Token compliance** — every colour/font/radius on screen traces to the
189	  locked tokens or Tier 1/2 derivation; no demoted-skill hex (gate 60).
190	
191	---
192	
193	## Our extra checks
194	
195	**Skeleton test.** From impeccable `bolder.md`: *"Strip the copy out of your
196	planned section and study the bare structure. Does the skeleton still say what
197	this section is and why it matters, through hierarchy and the system's devices
198	alone? If it only works once the words return, the boldness is in the text
199	size, not the design."* Run it on any section scored flat. The upstream
200	addendum matters as much as the test: *"a placeholder for an image or artifact
201	names a job, an anchor and a piece of evidence, not a cue to drop in a
202	decorative photo."*
203	
204	A section that fails the skeleton test is usually one that *"quietly opts out of
205	the system's own strongest moves"* — the page has a motif, a display scale and a
206	structural device, and this section uses none of them. That diagnosis routes to
207	`bolder`, and the fix is amplification in the system's own vocabulary, never a
208	new colour, face, or primitive. Name the route in the fix list.
209	
210	**Three litmus tests.** Image, card, brand — full text in
211	[`slop-test.md`](../slop-test.md) § Three litmus tests. The builder runs them on
212	their own output; here they are scored. Image test failures land under
213	Composition, card test failures under Composition, brand test failures under
214	Brand consistency. A litmus failure is at least P2: it means an element is on
215	the page carrying nothing.
216	
217	**Squint test.** Blur the screenshot 5px (or genuinely squint). Two
218	questions: does the hierarchy still read with the content gone, and **is any
219	column carrying less visual weight than its width claims** — a rail or a
220	9-column block holding only a couple of whispered lines? An open column that
221	fails this is a hole, not a rail; the fix is to weight it (numeral, stat,
222	image, full-height rule) or close it. This is Step 5 point 2 of
223	[`../../SKILL.md`](../../SKILL.md), applied here as a composition check
224	rather than a build-verification step.
225	
226	**Three-flat-text-sections contract.** From the composition contract in
227	[`../../SKILL.md`](../../SKILL.md) and the structural section of
228	[`house-physics.md`](../house-physics.md): scan the full-page slices for three
229	consecutive sections that are all plain text blocks with no anatomy variety —
230	no image, no ledger, no inversion, no grid-break. Three in a row is a fail
231	regardless of how good any single section is individually; flag it under
232	Composition and name the section range.
233	
234	---
235	
236	## Common failure patterns per dimension
237	
238	The upstream `critique-*` skills each close with a short list of what actually
239	goes wrong in that dimension. They were dropped in the first port; restored
240	here verbatim, 33 patterns across the seven dimensions. Read the list for the
241	dimension you are scoring *before* writing the observation — a named pattern is
242	a finding you can cite, and "the spacing feels off" is not.
243	
244	**Hierarchy** — multiple competing primaries, nothing reads as most important ·
245	hierarchy flattening, levels too similar in size, weight or colour · false
246	emphasis, decorative elements outweighing functional ones · buried CTA, the
247	action visually quieter than the content around it.
248	
249	**Composition** — equal-weight two-column layout with no clear
250	primary/secondary split · inconsistent padding, some components at 16px, others
251	at 20 or 24 with no system · orphaned elements floating without proximity to
252	their group · overcrowded sections adjacent to empty ones, creating
253	unintentional visual cliffs · competing horizontal rules and dividers that
254	multiply without adding structure.
255	
256	**Typography** — scale drift, sizes nudged by 1–2px instead of moving to the
257	next defined step · line-height mismatches, display sizes with body line-height
258	and the reverse · alignment mixing, centred headings above left-aligned body
259	with no intentional justification · hardcoded font sizes because the token was
260	not found or not updated · over-use of bold, more than two weight levels active
261	on one screen diluting contrast.
262	
263	**Colour** — link colour failing 4.5:1 against white once the underline is
264	removed · error states carried in red only, with no supporting icon or label ·
265	placeholder text at 40 % opacity failing contrast on light surfaces · one-off
266	hex values outside the token system · interactive and non-interactive elements
267	sharing one colour treatment.
268	
269	**Affordance** — ghost buttons in low-contrast contexts where the border becomes
270	invisible · focus rings suppressed with `outline: none` and no replacement ·
271	multiple filled CTAs leaving the reader unsure which to press · edit and delete
272	hidden behind hover, *"inaccessible on touch and invisible until discovered by
273	accident"* · empty states that explain nothing and offer no path forward.
274	
275	**Information density** — screens that show every available metric instead of
276	the most actionable · detail pages that inline all related objects instead of
277	linking · tables with 10+ columns where 3 do 90 % of the work · forms showing
278	all fields at once where a multi-step flow would reduce perceived complexity ·
279	content-heavy onboarding front-loading explanation before the reader has done
280	anything.
281	
282	**Brand consistency** — hardcoded values drifting from tokens over time · copy
283	written without consulting voice guidelines, defaulting to generic UI language ·
284	imagery sourced outside the brand mood reference · inconsistent radius or shadow
285	values across components on the same screen.
286	
287	**The fast path.** When the ask is functional rather than visual — a PM-led
288	review, a quick loop, "does this work" rather than "is this good" — run
289	dimensions **1, 5 and 6 only** (hierarchy, affordance, density): the three most
290	likely to block task completion. Say that you ran the fast path and which four
291	dimensions were not scored. This is upstream's `/critique-ux`, and it is a
292	declared narrowing, never a silent one.
293	
294	---
295	
296	## Scoring: heuristics, cognitive load, personas
297	
298	These three run alongside the seven dimensions and give the critique a number
299	that survives between rounds.
300	
301	**Nielsen 0–4, with honest `n/a`.** Score all ten heuristics 0–4 in a table with
302	a key issue per row. *"Be honest with scores. A 4 means genuinely excellent.
303	Most real interfaces score 20–32 out of 40."* Heuristics **7 (Flexibility and
304	Efficiency)** and **10 (Help and Documentation)** may be scored `n/a` on
305	Persuade and Experience surfaces — landing pages, campaigns, portfolios — as may
306	any heuristic that genuinely cannot apply. Write `n/a` with a one-line reason
307	and **renormalise the total to the applicable maximum**: 24/32, not 24/40.
308	*"Never print /40 over a partial set."* Read the band off the percentage when
309	the set is partial: 90 %+ excellent, 70 %+ good, 50 %+ acceptable, 30 %+ poor.
310	
311	**Cognitive load, eight items.** Score dimension 6 against this checklist and
312	count the failures — *"0–1 failures = low cognitive load (good). 2–3 = moderate
313	(address soon). 4+ = high cognitive load (critical fix needed)."*
314	
315	- **Single focus** — can the reader complete the primary task without
316	  distraction from competing elements?
317	- **Chunking** — is information in digestible groups (≤ 4 items per group)?
318	- **Grouping** — are related items visually grouped (proximity, borders, shared
319	  background)?
320	- **Visual hierarchy** — is it immediately clear what is most important?
321	- **One thing at a time** — can the reader focus on a single decision before the
322	  next?
323	- **Minimal choices** — ≤ 4 visible options at any decision point.
324	- **Working memory** — does the reader need to remember something from a
325	  previous screen to act on this one?
326	- **Progressive disclosure** — is complexity revealed only when needed?
327	
328	The ceiling behind it: *"Humans can hold ≤ 4 items in working memory at once"*
329	(Miller, revised by Cowan 2001). 5–7 is pushing the boundary; 8+ and readers
330	skip, misclick, or abandon.
331	
332	**Personas, chosen by surface type.** Walk the primary action as each and report
333	*specific* red flags — *"name the exact elements and interactions that fail each
334	persona. Don't write generic persona descriptions; write what broke for them."*
335	On a landing page the three are **mandatory**, because upstream's selection
336	table names them for marketing surfaces (first impressions, trust, mobile):
337	
338	- **Jordan (confused first-timer)** — icon-only navigation, jargon with no
339	  explanation, no visible help, ambiguous next step after an action, no
340	  confirmation that something worked. *"Is the first action obviously clear
341	  within 5 seconds?"*
342	- **Riley (deliberate stress tester)** — long strings, empty states, unexpected
343	  input, refresh mid-flow, features that look like they work and silently do
344	  not, error handling that leaves the UI broken.
345	- **Casey (distracted mobile user)** — thumb zone, state preserved across an
346	  interruption, slow connection, tap targets ≥ 44×44 and not crowded, heavy
347	  assets on every view.
348	
349	Alex (power user) and Sam (accessibility-dependent) are the dashboard and
350	data-heavy picks; Sam's ground is covered more rigorously by
351	`Skill(a11y-audit)`, so cite that rather than re-deriving it here.
352	
353	**Trend, not just a score.** Persist the report and read the last five runs so
354	the number means something:
355	
356	```bash
357	node ~/.agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/critique-storage.mjs write "<target>" <body-file>
358	node ~/.agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/critique-storage.mjs trend "<target>" 5
359	```
360	
361	Print one line after the report: `Trend for <slug> (last 5 runs): 24 → 28 → 32 →
362	29 → 32 (out of 40)`. When the runs used different applicable maxima, print each
363	score with its own denominator (`24/32 → 30/40`) and say plainly that the runs
364	scored different heuristic sets, so the line is not like-for-like. First run for
365	a slug: say so, no trend yet. This is fire-and-forget — a storage failure prints
366	an error and never blocks the critique.
367	
368	---
369	
370	## When the target is a change, not a screen
371	
372	A branch, a PR, or an uncommitted diff is a different job, and three upstream
373	rules keep it honest. (Scope resolution itself belongs to
374	[`review.md`](review.md) § 1; these are the critique-side traps.)
375	
376	**Read the removed side.** `removed-signals.md` lists what to look for on the
377	`-` side of a hunk, because a regression is invisible in the post-change state.
378	A row is a lead, never a finding: route it to its owner and report it only once
379	that owner confirms the interface got worse.
380	
381	| Removed | Owner | What to check |
382	|---|---|---|
383	| `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-live`, `role=` | a11y | Control or region lost its accessible name, description, or announcement |
384	| `alt=`, `<label`, `for=`, `scope=` | a11y | Image, field, or table cell lost its programmatic association |
385	| `<button>`, `<a>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<ul>` replaced by `div`/`span` | a11y | Keyboard and AT behaviour traded for styling |
386	| `:focus-visible`, `:focus`, `outline`, `tabindex` | a11y | Focus indicator gone, or the element left the tab order |
387	| Logical properties swapped for `left`/`right` | layout | Direction-aware layout dropped |
388	| `lang=`, `dir=` | typography | Language metadata or text direction dropped |
389	| `text-wrap`, `line-clamp`, `overflow-wrap`, `tabular-nums`, `font-feature-settings` | typography | Text rendering, wrapping, or numeral alignment silently changed |
390	| A colour token swapped for a literal, or for a lighter token | colour | The rendered contrast pair may now fail; measure it |
391	| A user-facing string deleted or shortened | writing | A label, error, or empty state lost the information it carried |
392	
393	Upstream's table carries one further row, covering two removed media features.
394	**F-011 (2026-09-07): the `prefers-reduced-motion` half of that row does not apply here — a build with no rm branch is correct in this system, so its removal is never a finding.**
395	The `prefers-contrast` half of the row stands and is routed to accessibility as
396	upstream has it.
397	
398	Check the **equivalent replacements** before routing anything, *"or the report
399	fills with refactors reported as regressions"*: `aria-label` giving way to
400	`aria-labelledby` pointing at visible text; an explicit `role` dropped because
401	the element became the native equivalent; `outline` replaced by a `box-shadow`
402	ring that still meets the focus rule; `tabindex="0"` dropped from something now
403	natively focusable; a literal replaced by a token that measures the same pair; a
404	physical property replaced by its logical counterpart; a string moved into the
405	translation catalogue rather than deleted.
406	
407	**Two exclusion traps under-exclude silently.** `*.lock` catches `yarn.lock` and
408	`Cargo.lock` but *not* `package-lock.json` or `pnpm-lock.yaml`. And `**` needs
409	glob magic: without it `*` never crosses `/`, so `**/dist/**` excludes
410	`packages/a/dist/` and misses a root-level `dist/`. Run the diff with and
411	without the pathspecs and confirm the count dropped by exactly the files you
412	named. Two exceptions stay in scope even though they look like assets: a **font
413	file** added or swapped is a typography change, and an **image** added to a
414	component is a UI and accessibility change through its `alt` and its outline.
415	
416	**Hold the change to its stated intent.** Read the title, body, linked issue and
417	commit messages, then review whether the interface delivers what they claim.
418	*"This is what surfaces the incomplete change, because a surface review inspects
419	the states that are present, and here the point is the ones that are absent"*:
420	
421	- a new variant, size, or theme applied to some states but not all — hover,
422	  focus, active, disabled, loading, selected;
423	- a new user-facing string with no entry in the translation catalogue;
424	- a new component with no empty, loading, error, disabled, or narrow-width state;
425	- a control added to one surface but not to the siblings that already carry its
426	  peers.
427	
428	*"Do not report scope creep. Whether a change does too much is a process
429	question, not an interface one."*
430	
431	**Evidence, not taste.** The bar for reporting is evidence; the bar for a clean
432	verdict is that you inspected what you claim to have inspected. *"A short report
433	from a real inspection beats a long one padded to look thorough."* Press hard on
434	the triggers, leave deliberate project choices alone — *"a density, radius, or
435	voice you merely disagree with is not a finding."* And keep the two sides
436	symmetric: **do not report a code-level finding from appearance alone, or a
437	visual finding from source alone** when runtime behaviour decides the result.
438	Every finding cites what it was read from.
439	
440	---
441	
442	## Output
443	
444	**1. Prioritised fix list**, P1/P2/P3, each tagged with its dimension:
445	
446	- **P1 — Critical**: breaks usability, accessibility, brand compliance, or a
447	  named gate; fix before shipping.
448	- **P2 — Important**: degrades the read or creates inconsistency; fix this
449	  pass.
450	- **P3 — Polish**: minor refinement; address when capacity allows.
451	
452	Each item: **Issue** (what's wrong) · **Dimension** (Hierarchy / Composition /
453	Typography / Colour / Affordance / Density / Brand) · **Fix** (the specific
454	change).
455	
456	**2. Craft gap table.** One row per element where the build and the locked
457	direction disagree — the format designpowers uses so a craft finding is as
458	checkable as a contrast ratio:
459	
460	| Element | Expectation (lock / register) | Current state | Gap |
461	|---|---|---|---|
462	| [element] | [what the reference lock or register calls for] | [what is on screen] | [the specific difference] |
463	
464	*"Evaluate craft, not just compliance."* The sentence upstream offers as the
465	model for this verdict is worth copying in shape (re-punctuated to keep gate 75
466	clean): *"This meets the plan requirements but the execution is flat."* Then the
467	defects, named: the shadows are uniform, the spacing has no rhythm, and the
468	colour usage does not match the restrained palette. Three named defects, one
469	verdict. "It doesn't feel right" is not a finding; name the gap.
470	
471	If no reference lock exists for this build, say so in one line — craft is then
472	judged against the register table and house physics only, and the table's
473	Expectation column says which.
474	
475	**3. One-paragraph assessment** naming the strongest dimension and the
476	weakest, in plain language a reviewer could check against the same
477	screenshots.
478	
479	**4. The honest reference sentence.** State plainly whether this page beats
480	every reference named in Step 1b — not "stands up beside them." If you cannot
481	say it beats them, say what specifically the references still do better and
482	tag it into the fix list. This is the Exit bar's reference claim, restated as
483	critique's own closing line.
484	
485	**Critique never edits.** It is a read on pixels, not a rewrite. Fixes named
486	here are a separate pass — hand the list to `build` or `polish`
487	([`../../SKILL.md`](../../SKILL.md) Step 0a), don't apply them inline.
