#### V3c · Plåt i grunden · kortet vänds

*Iteration av V3b, inte nytt bygge: registrets V3-rad uppdateras till V3c; fingerprint-gaten (≥4/6) gäller K3/K4, inte V3c.* Grundkonceptet och estetiken är låsta: kontinuerlig svartvit grund (`k4-cabin-desk.webp`), R5-världen vänster (Geist, `#0b0c0e`/`#1e5e9c`), R6-världen höger (Public Sans, `#fdfbf4`), rubriken utanför platen i affischskala, Hyperborea-platen som bleeder, ordscrubben i liggaren, Calyx/Hōrai live.

**Heron blir en pinnad akt.** `section.hero` får `data-sc-act="pin" data-sc-span="2.2" data-sc-dwell="0.35"` (var `flow`), med motorns stage-markup från `template.html` (aldrig restylade `.sc-*`-klasser, AB06). Rubriken, platen och underraden är stagens *ground* (synliga från p = 0; "ground or greet" uppfyllt utan cue). Ingen scroll-cue-text (gate 88).

**Kortet.** `figure.hero-plate` (samma storlek: `width:min(100% − 2·rail, 56vh·16/9)`, 16:9, vänsteranknuten vid `--rail-x`) får `perspective: 1600px`. Inuti: `.plate-card{position:absolute;inset:0;transform-style:preserve-3d;transform:rotateY(calc(var(--flip,0) * -180deg))}` med två `.face` (`backface-visibility:hidden`, hairline `--frame-line`). **Framsidan** = dagens innehåll (logo-dock + `#heroPoolImg`; ljuspölen vandrar vidare, nu på `--sc-ps`). **Baksidan** (`transform:rotateY(180deg)`, `background:var(--c-black)`): `ALUNIX` i Geist 700, `clamp(3.2rem, 9cqw, 7.5rem)`, `line-height:.9`, uppercase (displayskala ≥ 5× body, TASTE §2.4); under: `Digital byrå` som kicker (Geist Mono 10.5 px, .22 em; en av sidans ≤ 4 monoetiketter); hairline; raden `Design  Utveckling  System` i samma monoregister (samma ordning som liggaren 01–03, så att de två listorna inte motsäger varandra; **öppen fråga till Anton**: hans meddelande listade "utveckling, design, system", är ordningen avsiktlig?); `Boka ett möte →` som typsatt länk (Geist 700, understruken i accent). **Ingen tidsstämpel, ingen `2026 · SVERIGE`, ingen lede** (underraden under platen bär redan leden; två leder i folden vore dubbelt).

**Koreografin på `--sc-ps`** (aldrig rå `--sc-p`): `flip = smoothstep(0.12, 0.72, ps)` i sidans JS (skrivs som `--flip` på `.plate-card`); p 0–0,12 stilla, ljuspölen vandrar; 0,12–0,72 vändningen (Y-axeln, som ett visitkort man vänder med handen; vid 90° syns bara hairlinen, det är ärligt); 0,72–1 baksidan i vila, dwell låter den landa. `will-change:transform` sätts på `.plate-card` bara medan `0 < ps < 1` och tas bort i vila. Båda riktningarna. `?preview=back` tvingar `--flip:1`. Rubriken står kvar hela tiden (stagens ground); underraden också.

**Under heron.** `section.panel-open` (svarta konsolkortet) **tas bort**; dess innehåll bor nu på kortets baksida. `section.panel-services` (Tjänster, tre lika kolumner 01–03) **tas bort** som dubblett av liggaren (och gate 3-familj). Ny kolumnfördelning, materialväxling i båda spalterna (TASTE §4.5): **vänster** = blå tes (Hyperborea-bleed) → Calyx (ljus iframe) → **pris** (mörk); **höger** = jätterubrik + liggare (papper) → Hōrai (mörk iframe). `calyx-wrap` behåller `flex:1`. Arkitekten läser kolumnvikten som pixlar (squint: ingen kolumn får bära mindre vikt än sin bredd) och får flytta priset tillbaka till höger om vänster blir för tung.

**Lyftet i V3c (utan att ändra konceptet):** allt bespoke (`paintMotion`, `paintHeroPool`, ordscrubben) läser `--sc-ps`; `.giant`:s permanenta `will-change` bort; preload av Geist 700 + Public Sans 300; `decoding="async"` + `fetchpriority="high"` på hero-bilden; `loading="lazy"` + IO-montering på iframes; `content-visibility:auto` på `.price`/`.horai-wrap`; `text-wrap: balance` på rubriker; hover/focus på de tre länkarna (`:focus-visible` 2 px offset ≥ 3:1 mot båda grunderna); hairlinerna på `--rail-x`-rastret; 320/375/414/768 verifierade (kortet blir 4:5 under 640 px som idag och vänds fortfarande); copy-gaten bara på de ändrade strängarna (ordagrann copy bevaras).

**Vad referenserna gör som V3c måste slå** (låses via `select.py`; förväntat: `garden-eight`, `mattis-studio`, `squarespace`, ev. `creative-giants`): Garden Eight: *ett typografiskt moment, ett skulpturalt moment, åtskilda av tystnad* → V3c:s hero får bara rubrik + kort + en rad, inget mer. Mattis: konsolkortet med hörnmarkeringar är platt → V3c:s kort är ett *fysiskt* kort som vänds. Squarespace: svarta/vita band med ett statistikblock → V3c:s inversioner ska vara lika rena, utan kort.

=====CONCEPTS 136-378=====
## V3c · Plåt i grunden · kortet vänds

### (1) Auktoritet och vad som viker

**Auktoriteten är typen** (TASTE § 1, raden "Typen (ordmärke eller rubrik i
viewport-bredd)"): rubriken `Er hemsida är nutidens visitkort` i affischgrad utanför
plåten bär sidan, och den står kvar genom hela den pinnade akten som stagens ground.

Vad som viker, en mening var: **fotot** viker genom att stanna lågexponerat inuti plåten
och aldrig gå fullbleed. **Ytan** viker genom att vara en enda kontinuerlig svartvit grund
utan sektionsfärger, så materialbytet sker i spalterna och inte i grunden. **Färgen**
viker genom att `#1e5e9c` bara gör en sak, den blå tesplåten, och aldrig blir knapp,
ram eller understryk. **Rörelsen** viker på hela sidan **utom i signaturakten**, där
TASTE § 4.8:s r6-precisering gäller: i set-piecet är rörelsen auktoriteten, och där är
typen redan vikt 300 och fotot redan lågexponerat.

**Mätningen som gör "ett displayelement" sant genom hela akten:** vid 1440 är plåten
`min(1440 - 2*rail, 56vh*16/9)` = 896 px bred, och kortbaksidans `ALUNIX` klampar på
`9cqw` av plåtens egen container = 81 px (taket `7.5rem` = 120 px binder inte).
Hero-rubriken ligger på ~9cqw av sidans container = ~130 px. Kvoten är 0,62, alltså det
"ett steg ner" TASTE § 1 kräver, och 81 px mot 16 px brödtext är 5,1x, alltså över
TASTE § 2.4:s golv. **Byggaren mäter och rapporterar båda talen vid 1440; målvärde
kvot <= 0,70 och baksidans display >= 5x brödtexten.**

### (2) Troplistan, avprickad

TASTE § 5, punkt för punkt:

| Trop | V3c |
|---|---|
| Ikongrid | Frånvarande. Sidan har noll ikoner; tjänsterna är en liggare med siffror. |
| Gradient-mesh | Frånvarande. Grunden är ett fotografi, tonad genom `--sc-canvas`-drift, aldrig en gradient. |
| Glasmorfism | Frånvarande. Ingen `backdrop-filter` någonstans; `panel-open`, det svarta konsolkortet, **tas bort**. |
| Centrerad hero med badge-rad | Frånvarande. Rubriken är vänsterställd på `--rail-x`, ingen badge finns. |
| Lila/indigo-accent | Frånvarande. Enda accenten är `#1e5e9c`. |
| Skuggade 8 px-kort | Frånvarande. Noll `box-shadow`. Plåtens enda kant är en hårlinje `--frame-line`. **Radie 0 överallt** (Shape Consistency Lock, skalan {0-3}). |
| Stockfoto av leende team | Frånvarande. Inga människor, inga ansikten, inga händer. |
| "h1 48 / h2 32"-skala | Frånvarande. Display 130 px / 81 px mot brödtext 16 px; inget ligger på mellannivån. |
| Dekorativa blobbar | Frånvarande. |
| Tre lika feature-kort | Frånvarande. `panel-services` **tas bort** som dubblett av liggaren, vilket är hela skälet. |

Utöver listan:

- **F-006 (glaskort med telemetri över foto):** frånvarande. Det svarta konsolkortet med
  `2026 · SVERIGE` och den levande klockan är den närmaste släktingen på V3b och det är
  precis den sektion V3c tar bort. Kortbaksidan får **ingen tidsstämpel och ingen
  `2026 · SVERIGE`**, uttryckligen enligt målbilden.
- **Gate 47 (re-drawn chrome):** frånvarande. De tre exempelsajterna visas i riktiga
  `<iframe>`, aldrig i en ritad webbläsarram, och kortet har ingen ram som imiterar UI.
  **Risken sitter i själva kortmetaforen:** ett "visitkort" med hårlinje är ett fysiskt
  objekt, inte en ritad UI-ram, och skiljer sig från Mattis konsolram genom att det saknar
  hörnmarkeringar, versionstagg och klocka. Byggaren får inte lägga tillbaka någon av dem.
- **Gate 79 (fabricerad produkt-UI):** frånvarande. Ingenting på sidan simulerar en skärm.
- **Gate 88 (scroll-cue):** frånvarande, och uttryckligen: stagens ground är synlig från
  p = 0, så "ground or greet" är uppfyllt utan cue-text.

### (3) Ett displayelement per skärm (1440x900)

| Skärm | Vad som syns | Displayelementet | Allt annat |
|---|---|---|---|
| s1 | Hero vid ps = 0: rubrik i affischgrad, kortets framsida med ljuspölen, underraden under plåten | `Er hemsida är nutidens visitkort` (~130 px) | Plåten lågexponerad, underraden 16 px, logo-docken i registergrad |
| s2 | Hero vid ps ~ 0,42: kortet mitt i vändningen, rubriken kvar | **Vändningen själv** (TASTE § 4.8, r6-preciseringen: rörelsen bär set-piecet) | Rubriken kvar men vikt 300, ingen ny text tillkommer |
| s3 | Hero vid ps >= 0,72: kortbaksidan i vila, rubriken kvar | `ALUNIX` på baksidan (81 px, kvot 0,62 mot rubriken) | Kicker `Digital byrå` 10,5 px, hårlinje, tjänsteraden i mono, `Boka ett möte ->` som typsatt länk |
| s4 | Vänster: blå tesplåt med Hyperborea-bleeden. Höger: jätterubriken över liggarens rad 01 | `VI BYGGER ERT VARUMÄRKE.` i högerspalten | Tesargumentet i brödgrad, Hyperborea-plåtens bildtext i registergrad |
| s5 | Vänster: Calyx som ljus iframe. Höger: liggarens rader 02-03 som scrubbas fram | Calyx-ramen (den levande sajten är skärmens objekt) | Liggarraderna är registergrad med siffror, aldrig display |
| s6 | Vänster: prisblocket, mörkt. Höger: Hōrai som mörk iframe | `Alla har rätt till bra design.` | Prisraderna som fetstilsrader i brödgrad, paketpriserna som liggarsiffror |
| s7 | Avslut: `kontakt@alunix.se` som textrad mot grunden | Mailto-raden, ensam på skärmen | Ingenting annat; ingen formulärkomponent, ingen upprepad CTA |

Sju skärmar. Total scrollhöjd: heron 2,2 span + 0,35 dwell = ~2,55 vh, plus sex
flow-skärmar, landar i intervallet 9-11 vh, inom budgeten 8-14 vh
(`feel-and-fingerprint.md` § Pacing).

**Kolumnviktsvarning som lead ska squinta på efter R2:** s6 lägger prisblocket (mörkt,
tungt) i vänsterspalten samtidigt som högerspalten bär Hōrai (också mörk). Målbilden ger
arkitekten rätt att flytta priset tillbaka till höger om vänster blir för tung. Domen
skjuts till pixelläsningen; ingen kolumn får bära mindre vikt än sin bredd.

### (4) Registerraden för V3 -> V3c (förslag; lead för in den efter Antons dom)

Fingerprint-gaten (>= 4/6) gäller **inte** V3c: cellen är en iteration av V3b och tar över
registrets V3-linje i stället för att öppna en ny yta. Radformatet är
`feel-and-fingerprint.md` § Row format.

```
| r8 V3c Plåt i grunden, kortet vänds | Continuous world, loose reading inherited from M1 via V3b | Thin top row with wordmark and contact that scrolls away, inherited chrome | The same framed plate, now a two-faced card in a pinned act: headline outside it at poster scale, subline under it, and the plate itself turning on its Y axis from photographic front to matte black back | 7 screens, 1 pinned act (span 2.2, dwell 0.35) plus 6 flow acts; panel-open and panel-services removed, their content moved onto the card's back and into the ledger; two columns that swap material against each other | The price ledger and a mailto set as a line of type, no form, no repeated CTA | The hero plate is a physical card: `--flip = smoothstep(0.12, 0.72, --sc-ps)` turns `.plate-card` on rotateY so the light-pool front becomes a matte black back carrying the wordmark, hairline only at 90 degrees | Cinematic dark | Geist + Public Sans; `--sc-canvas` #0b0c0e, paper #fdfbf4, accent #1e5e9c | `anti-slop-design/tests/alunix-r8/runs/V3c/index.html` |
```

**Varför detta fortfarande är en iteration och inte ett nytt bygge.** Grammatik, nav,
värld, palett och typsnitt är oförändrade från V3b, och de tre dimensioner som ändras
(hero-device, aktform, signatur) ändras alla av **samma** ingrepp: plåten blir ett kort med
två sidor. Ett nytt bygge skulle ha ändrat minst en av grammatik, nav eller värld; V3c
ändrar ingen av dem. Registrets V3-linje är därmed fortfarande upptagen av samma yta, nu
med en mer specifik signatur. Två saker tas dessutom **bort** utan att ersättas av något
nytt (`panel-open`, `panel-services`), vilket är iterationens signatur, inte nybyggets.

### (5) Rörelsen

**Motion-tes.**

- **Focal:** ögat äger plåtens mittlinje. Vändningen sker runt plåtens egen vertikala
  mittaxel, så det som rör sig är exakt det som redan var i fokus vid ps = 0.
- **Continuity:** rubriken och underraden står stilla genom hela akten. De är stagens
  ground och de är kontinuitetsankaret som gör att vändningen läses som att *kortet*
  vänds och inte som att sidan byter scen.
- **Feedback:** varje scrollhack flyttar `--flip` med en lerpad andel, så handen får
  omedelbart svar; vid 90 grader syns bara hårlinjen, vilket är det ärliga svaret på
  "var är kortet nu".
- **Budget:** en pinnad akt på hela sidan, span 2,2 + dwell 0,35. Ingen annan akt får
  `pin`. Sidans övriga sex skärmar är `flow` med korta stagger.

### (6) Färgstrategi

**Nivå: Restrained.** Sidan är en kontinuerlig svartvit fotografisk grund plus papper, och
exakt en kromatisk färg som gör exakt en sak.

**Den fysiska scenen, i en mening:** ett mörkt rum där ett enda visitkort ligger på ett
bord under en snedställd lampa, och där ljuset längre in i sidan faller på en pappersark
i stället.

**Låset, utskrivet, inget nytt val görs:** målbilden låser paletten till `#0b0c0e`
(grunden), `#fdfbf4` (papperet, R6-världen), `#1e5e9c` (accenten) och typsnitten till
**Geist** (röst: kortbaksidans ordmärke, liggarrubrikerna, den typsatta länken; Geist Mono
enbart som register, max fyra monoetiketter på sidan) och **Public Sans** (hero-rubriken i
vikt 300, jätterubriken, brödtext). Rollerna korsar aldrig. Ingen tredje familj.
Font-proceduren i `brand.md` körs inte om: valet är ärvt från en godkänd cell och att
öppna det vore ett nytt bygge, inte en iteration.

**Accentens frekvenstal, skrivet som ett tal och inte som en känsla** (lånat från
`dope-security`): `#1e5e9c` förekommer **två** gånger på sidan: tesplåtens grund
(`data-sc-drift="#123f68"` är dess mörkare drift-mål, samma roll) och understrykningen i
`Boka ett möte ->` på kortbaksidan. Ingen tredje förekomst. Aldrig som ram, aldrig som
knappfyllning, aldrig i liggaren.

### (7) Vad referenserna gör som cellen måste slå

Ingen kicker, ingen cue, ingen tidsstämpel, ingen andra CTA. Mätbart: `preflight_taste.py` hero-regeln, textelement <= 4 |

Mätbart: vid ps = 0,5 syns hårlinjen och ingenting annat av kortet |
| `squarespace` (målbildens ribba, planens § 7.5) | Svarta och vita band som byter genom skala, inte genom färg, med ett statistikblock och noll accent | V3c:s inversioner ska vara lika rena och göras **utan ett enda kort**: materialbytet sker i spalten själv (blått block, papper, mörkt prisblock), och det enda "statistikblocket" är tre sanna priser |

Framsidan måste bära **material över hela ytan** och en ljusrespons som ändras med vinkeln. Detta är exakt fyndet i F-007-kontrollen nedan |

### (8) Rut-testet

**Kategorins default för "digital byrå", i tre rader**, hållen utanför:

1. Centrerad hero med en badge över rubriken, en fylld primärknapp och en spökknapp
   bredvid, ovanpå en mörk gradient eller ett suddigt kontorsfoto.
2. En logotypvägg med kundmärken, tre lika tjänstekort med ikoner, och en sifferrad med
   "200+ projekt / 15 år / 98 % nöjda kunder".
3. Ett citat med porträtt och ett kontaktformulär i botten, plus en sticky knapp som följer
   med hela vägen.

Var målbilden möter defaulten, och vad som ändras:

| Punkt där målbilden riskerar defaulten | Vad som ändras |
|---|---|
| **Tre tjänster.** Byråer räknar alltid upp tre tjänster; V3b gjorde det två gånger (liggaren och `panel-services`) | `panel-services` **tas bort**. Kvar är liggaren, som är rader med siffror på papper, inte kort med ikoner. Och tjänsteorden repeteras en tredje gång på kortbaksidan, men i **monoregister på 10,5 px**, alltså som en signatur och inte som en tjänstelista |
| **En CTA i heron.** Defaulten sätter "Boka ett möte" som en fylld knapp direkt under rubriken | `Boka ett möte ->` finns bara på **kortets baksida**, alltså först efter att besökaren scrollat genom hela akten, och den är en **typsatt länk** med understrykning i accenten, inte en knapp. Ingen sticky CTA finns |
| **Ordmärket i heron.** Defaulten sätter loggan uppe till vänster i en navrad | Ordmärket finns två gånger: i den tunna toppraden som scrollar bort, och i affischgrad på kortets baksida. Den andra förekomsten är hela akten's poäng, inte chrome |
| **Sifferraden.** Defaulten fyller ut med tal | V3c har **noll** tal utom de tre priserna, som är sanna. TASTE § 4.9 tillåter formen bara med sant innehåll |
| **Kontaktformuläret** | Ersatt av `kontakt@alunix.se` som en textrad och en mailto. Inget formulär, inget fält, ingen skickaknapp |
| **Mörk gradient som grund** | Ersatt av ett kontinuerligt fotografi i gråskala som tonas via `--sc-canvas`-drift. Materialet är en riktig yta, inte en färgövergång |

## F-007-kontrollen av hero-plattans nuvarande stillbild

Läst som pixlar: `tests/alunix-concepts-r3/build/assets/k1-stage-pool.webp` (1600x1067,
65 kB) och den byggda folden `tests/alunix-concepts-r5/cells/V3b-chain/shots/desktop-1440--fold.png`.

**Dom: nej, ljuspölen bär inte flippen.** Tre mätbara skäl, i fallande materialitet:

1. **Fram- och baksida delar värde.** Cirka 60 % av bildens yta (hela övre bandet och
   högra tredjedelen) ligger på eller nära ren svart, och baksidan är
   `background: var(--c-black)`. Vändningen går alltså från "svart rektangel" till
   "svart rektangel med text". Det ögat ska läsa som två sidor av ett kort läser som
   samma sida två gånger.
2. **Ingen kant och ingen struktur att förkorta.** Motivet är en mjuk, kantlös ellips av
   ljus på tyg. En Y-rotation blir läsbar genom att raka linjer och kanter förkortas i

   mätt: där bär korkens kant och spräckliga material hela rotationen.
3. **Logo-docken sitter på död svart.** I den byggda folden ligger ordmärket i plåtens
   övre vänstra hörn, på ett parti utan textur. Framsidan har alltså inget material där
   ögat landar först.

6	
7	# Accessibility audit
8	
9	Eight passes over the target, in order. Each pass produces evidence; the report in pass 8 is only as good as what was actually inspected. `references/principles.md` holds the full principle catalog this procedure draws on, tagged by source. `references/report-template.md` holds the exact report skeleton.
10	
11	**Standing override — F-011 (Anton, 2026-09-07, permanent, global — applies to every audit this skill runs, not just one project):** motion always plays. Do not raise a finding, escalation, or debt-ledger item for an animation, autoplay, or scroll set-piece that ignores `prefers-reduced-motion` or any other browser/OS motion-accessibility signal — that is intentional in every design system this skill audits, not a defect. This is a deliberate, informed trade against real accessibility guidance (vestibular-disorder / motion-sensitivity users lose their opt-out); it is not an oversight, so do not "helpfully" flag it anyway. Every other WCAG check still applies in full, including the hard, preference-independent seizure-safety limit (no content flashing more than three times per second, WCAG 2.3.1) — that one is not a preference, it stays enforced regardless.
12	
13	## 0 · Scope + coverage
14	
15	State what you're auditing (URL, files, or a static screenshot set) and what that lets you verify. A static screenshot verifies visual and content findings only — keyboard, screen-reader, and focus-order findings are **inferred, never verified**, and the report must say so.
16	
17	| Input | Verified | Inferred |
18	| --- | --- | --- |
19	| Live URL / running build | Mechanical scripts, keyboard, focus, contrast, reflow, motion | — |
20	| Static screenshot(s) | Visual contrast (against the pixels shown), content, layout | Keyboard path, screen-reader announcement, focus order, states not shown |
21	| Source files, no runtime | Semantics in markup, ARIA, labels-in-code | Rendered contrast, computed focus styles, actual tab order |
22	
23	Never claim coverage you didn't inspect. Say "inferred from static image" or "not verified — no browser" rather than silently upgrading a guess to a finding.
24	
25	## 1 · Mechanical pass
26	
27	Run the scripts and read every JSON field before writing findings from them.
28	
29	```bash
30	python <S>/scripts/a11y_scan.py <url>     # <S> = this skill's own directory
31	python <S>/scripts/tab_walk.py <url> [--max 200]
32	python <S>/scripts/reflow.py <url>
33	python ~/.agents/skills/design/scripts/contrast.py <url>
34	python ~/.agents/skills/design/scripts/contrast_over_media.py <url>
35	```
36	
37	- **`a11y_scan.py`** — axe-core at desktop (1440×900) and mobile (390×844), merged. Returns `{url, violations: [{id, impact, description, help, viewports, nodes}], passes, incomplete}`. Each violation carries the WCAG tags axe matched it to.
38	- **`tab_walk.py`** — walks the page with real `Tab` presses. Returns `{stops, issues}` where each issue is `empty_name`, `offscreen`, `order_mismatch`, `no_focus_indicator`, `positive_tabindex`, `focus_trap`, or `unreachable_interactive` (a click handler with no keyboard path).
39	- **`reflow.py`** — three checks: overflow at 320px width, overflow at 200% zoom emulation, and **unrevealed content**: elements still `opacity: 0` at three scroll depths (a reveal system that never fires). Returns `{overflow320, overflowZoom200, unrevealed, unrevealedSelectors}`. Under F-011 there is no reduced-motion branch left to isolate, so check (c) is read purely as an unrevealed-content count — the AB09 failure where a page shipped empty below the fold.
40	- **`contrast.py`** / **`contrast_over_media.py`** — rendered-pixel contrast, the second for text over photo or video (worst-case patch, not the mean).
41	
42	**CARL rule.** Once per project, before trusting a clean pass from any of these five scripts, run them against `~/anti-slop-design/tests/a11y/broken.html` (absolute; the fixture lives in the design-system repo, not in the audited project) (a fixture with a known violation of each kind: missing label, no focus ring, un-reachable click handler, 320px overflow, failing contrast pair) and confirm every script actually reports it. A verifier that passes a broken page is worse than no verifier — it produces false confidence. If that file is missing, say so and create an equivalent fixture before relying on any script's silence as a clean bill. Hash-routed or multi-state pages: run the scripts once per state (`…/index.html#dashboard`, with the modal open) — the scripts only see the DOM they load.
43	
44	## 2 · POUR pass
45	
46	Walk Perceivable / Operable / Understandable / Robust. Cite the WCAG 2.2 AA success-criterion number on every finding (`compliance-mapping` tables in `references/principles.md` map design decisions to criteria — use them rather than guessing a number). Cross-reference `a11y_scan.py`'s violations here; each axe rule maps to one or more SC numbers axe already reports.
47	
48	## 3 · Cognitive pass (COGA)
49	
50	For each screen or step, rate the three loads — **intrinsic** (inherent to the task, reduce by chunking not by removing function), **extraneous** (added by the design, eliminate ruthlessly), **germane** (the user's actual engagement, protect it by removing the other two). Then check wayfinding's three questions hold at every point: **where am I, where can I go, how do I get back** — each answerable in under a second, without memory. Verify focus (one primary action per screen, interruptions controllable), error recovery (undo, confirmation on destructive actions, preserved input), and memory load (nothing the user must carry in their head between steps that the interface could show instead).
51	
52	Then rate every screen or step on six dimensions, with the thresholds — this is what turns "feels complex" into a finding:
53	
54	| Dimension | Low (good) | Medium (review) | High (redesign) |
55	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
56	| Decisions required | 0–1 | 2–3 | 4+ |
57	| Items to remember | none | 1–2 | 3+ |
58	| New concepts to learn | none | 1 | 2+ |
59	| Steps to complete | 1–2 | 3–5 | 6+ |
60	| Reading complexity | plain language | some jargon | dense / technical |
61	| Visual complexity | clean, focused | moderate | cluttered |
62	
63	**If any single dimension rates High, that screen needs redesign before launch** — the rating is not averaged across the six, exactly as an escalation trigger is never averaged down. Walk the flow as a user who is tired, stressed and unfamiliar; where you pause, re-read, or feel uncertain is a load spike, and the next question is whether the difficulty is intrinsic (chunk it) or extraneous (delete it). Report as a screen-by-screen table with the ratings, then recommendations sorted by impact.
64	
65	## 4 · Content pass
66	
67	Reading age 12–14 (grade 6–8; grade 4–6 for buttons, labels, and errors) — flag anything denser. Heading hierarchy: one H1, no skipped levels, headings that alone tell the page's story, and **depth never past H4** — a page reaching H5 has a structure problem, not a markup problem. Labels: every input has a visible, programmatic label; placeholders are never labels. Alt text by the decision table: decorative → `alt=""`; functional → the action; informative → the meaning; complex → short alt plus an extended description nearby; never "image of…". Link text stands alone out of context — no "click here" or "read more". Error messages follow **what happened + why + what to do**, in plain language, never blaming the user. Tables carry a caption and scoped headers, never used for layout. Multimedia: accurate synced captions (never unreviewed auto-captions), transcripts for audio, audio description for meaningful visual content, keyboard-accessible play / pause / stop / volume / seek controls.
68	
69	**Autoplay — the explicit ruling.** F-011 removes the *preference gate*, not the *control*. Two different things sit under the word "autoplay" and only one of them is overridden:
70	
71	| Case | Verdict |
72	| --- | --- |
73	| A silent, decorative video or scroll set-piece that starts on its own and ignores `prefers-reduced-motion` | **Not a finding.** F-011, by design. |
74	| **Audio** that starts on its own | **Finding, HIGH.** Audio is not motion; it collides with a screen reader and with whatever the person is listening to. WCAG 1.4.2 stands untouched. |
75	| Any autoplaying media with **no reachable pause / stop control** | **Finding.** The user must be able to stop it once it is running, and that control must be keyboard-reachable and labelled. Removing the preference gate did not remove the user's ability to act. |
76	| Content flashing more than three times per second | **Finding, HIGH.** Seizure safety, not a preference (WCAG 2.3.1). |
77	
78	## 5 · Adaptive pass
79	
80	Respect every system preference automatically, never ask the user to reconfigure what the OS already knows: `prefers-color-scheme` (real dark mode — dark grey not pure black, off-white not pure white), `prefers-contrast`, `prefers-reduced-transparency` (solid surfaces, no backdrop blur), `forced-colors`. `prefers-reduced-motion` is the one preference this skill does not audit — see the F-011 standing override above; everything else in this list is audited in full. Text in `rem`, never `px`; layout survives 200% zoom and reflows at 320px with no horizontal scroll; density has at least a comfortable default and never drops below 44×44 touch targets or 1.5 line-height at any level. Colour independence: every colour-carried meaning has a second encoding (icon, text, pattern, shape), and the interface passes the **greyscale test**. **In running prose, the underline is the accessible indicator and colour is the enhancement** — an inline link distinguished by colour alone fails colour independence no matter how strong the contrast; the design system's own styling clause on this is gate 61, and a link that drops the underline needs a second non-colour channel in its place (weight, a background, a marker), not a stronger hue. Run the greyscale test explicitly — convert the interface to greyscale and confirm status, errors, charts, and links are all still legible — and report the result rather than assuming it.
81	
82	## 6 · Interaction pass
83	
84	Native element first, ARIA last — `<button>` for actions, `<a href>` for navigation, never `<div onClick>`; no ARIA beats bad ARIA. Focus-visible ring at least 2px solid with 3:1 contrast against every adjacent colour it crosses, never bare `outline: none`. Hit areas: 24×24 CSS px is the WCAG 2.5.8 AA floor, 44×44 the touch target, 40×40 a reasonable desktop target; extend with a pseudo-element on the label or button, never overlapping another target. Every gesture (swipe, pinch, drag, long-press, shake) has a button-based alternative — gestures are shortcuts, never gatekeepers. Skip link is the first focusable element on any page with repeated navigation. Composite widgets (tabs, menus, toolbars) use roving tabindex — one Tab stop, active item `0`, the rest `-1`, arrow keys move both. Modals set `inert` on the background, trap focus inside, and return it to the trigger on close. **Landmarks: `banner`, `navigation`, `main`, `contentinfo` are the minimum on every page** — screen-reader users navigate by region before they navigate by heading, and a page with no regions is one undifferentiated run. Prefer the native elements (`<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<footer>`) over explicit `role=`; where a landmark type repeats (two navs, several significant forms), each instance carries a distinguishing `aria-label`. **Every `<iframe>` carries a `title`** — an untitled frame announces as "frame" and nothing more, and on a page embedding a map, a video, a preview or a live demo this is the single most likely automated finding. Both checks are cheap and both are routinely missing, because no build reference mentions them; `tab_walk.py` will not catch either, so check the markup. Never a positive `tabindex` anywhere. Paste is never blocked in any field — password managers and 2FA autofill depend on it — and every field about the user carries a meaningful `autocomplete`.
85	
86	## 7 · Persona walkthrough
87	
88	Build 4–6 personas spanning permanent, temporary, and situational conditions (not four permanent-disability personas and nothing else — a broken arm and a parent holding a baby belong in the set too). For each persona, walk every key task from the brief and record whether it **works**, **works with friction**, **works with workaround**, or **fails**. Compile into a barrier matrix: task × persona, one cell per combination. A task that fails for any persona is a finding regardless of how it looks for the rest.
89	
90	**Name the technology, not the disability.** "A blind user" produces a guess; "JAWS on Windows Firefox, navigating by headings" produces a walkthrough. Cover at minimum: one screen-reader user, one keyboard-only user, one low-vision user using magnification, one user with a cognitive difference, and one user in a situational-impairment context.
91	
92	The inventory to pick from:
93	
94	| Sense | Technologies, and what each one changes |
95	| --- | --- |
96	| Vision | **Screen reader** (JAWS, NVDA, VoiceOver, TalkBack) — reads aloud, navigates by headings, links and landmarks. **Magnifier** (ZoomText, OS zoom) — sees only a fraction of the screen at a time. **Braille display** — text to braille in real time, alongside a screen reader. **High-contrast mode** — system-level colour override. |
97	| Motor | **Switch device** — one or two buttons scanning through options; *much slower than a keyboard, and every extra step counts*. **Voice control** (Dragon, Voice Access) — spoken commands. **Head pointer / eye tracking** — limited precision. **Mouth stick / stylus**. |
98	| Hearing | Captions, visual alerts replacing audio ones, hearing loop / Bluetooth to hearing aids. |
99	| Cognitive | **Text-to-speech** (not a screen reader — the person sees the screen but processes better by hearing), reading ruler, simplified view, password managers as memory relief. |
100	
101	**The switch device is the worst case for anything long and pinned.** A page whose primary content is a several-screen scroll sequence with pinned acts costs a switch user one scan cycle per step, and there is no "skip to the end of the act" unless the build provides one. Walk that case explicitly rather than inferring it from the keyboard walkthrough.
102	
103	**Scenario template — eight fields**, and a scenario is not done until all eight are filled:
104	
105	```
106	Name:            [name]
107	Role/context:    [who they are beyond their disability]
108	Technology:      [devices, AT, browser, settings]
109	Environment:     [where, when, what else is happening]
110	Task:            [what they are trying to accomplish]
111	Steps:           [how they interact, step by step, using their AT]
112	Pain points:     [where the design fails or creates friction]
113	Success:         [what a good outcome looks like for this person]
114	```
115	
116	The scenario's job is to surface a specific failure a developer could fix — not to describe a goal. If it does not name a step where the design breaks, it hasn't been walked.
117	
118	Two source lists worth pulling from rather than inventing: `situational-impairment-mapping`'s permanent / temporary / situational split per sense (bright sunlight, a noisy train, gloves, one hand holding a child are the same barriers as their permanent counterparts), and `edge-case-identification`'s content cases — long hyphenated names, non-Latin scripts on a Swedish/English page, a single character, an empty value (`references/principles.md` carries both, tagged by source).
119	
120	## 8 · Report
121	
122	Assemble in `references/report-template.md`'s exact shape:
123	
124	- **Coverage table** from Step 0 — what was verified vs. inferred, restated with what actually got inspected.
125	- **Findings table** — `Severity | Location | Before | After | Why | WCAG | Who`. One row per root cause; list every location a systemic issue reaches. `Who` names the affected persona(s) or user group, not just "users".
126	- **Escalation triggers** — always `HIGH` the moment confirmed, never averaged down: no accessible name on an interactive control; a keyboard-reachable control with no visible focus indicator; a control reachable by pointer but not keyboard; content flashing more than three times per second (WCAG 2.3.1 — the one motion check that stays, preference-independent); content or a control clipped or unreachable at 320px width or 200% zoom; a contrast pair that fails its required ratio; state or meaning carried by colour alone; a destructive action with no confirmation or undo; truncated content with no way to reach the full value; content reachable only past a scroll edge or disclosure with no visible cue; an error that names no way to recover; a semantic colour used against its meaning.
127	- **Verdict** — `Block` when any `HIGH` remains, `Approve` otherwise. Never `Approve` coverage you did not inspect.
128	- **Legal map** — which of EAA/EN 301 549, ADA, Section 508, and WCAG 2.2 AA each finding touches. Most organisations target WCAG 2.2 AA; EAA (in effect since June 2025) and EN 301 549 align with it; ADA and Section 508 case law references it.
129	- **SEO flag** — mark findings on headings, alt text, `lang`, link text, or reflow as SEO-relevant; the same structural signals search crawlers and screen readers both depend on.
130	- **Deferred items** append to `.impeccable/a11y-debt.md` in the audited project — never dropped silently. Accepting accessibility debt requires the user's explicit acknowledgement in the conversation, not an assumed sign-off.
131	
132	### The debt-entry format — an eight-field ADR
133	
134	A one-line "deferred: contrast on the footer" is how a decision gets silently reversed two redesigns later by someone who wasn't in the room. Write each entry as a decision record (`inclusive/decision-documentation`):
135	
136	| Field | What goes in it |
137	| --- | --- |
138	| **Title** | Clear and searchable — "Form validation: inline errors instead of summary banner", not "form fix". |
139	| **Date and author** | When, and by whom. |
140	| **Context** | The situation and the constraints that produced the decision. |
141	| **Decision** | What was decided, specifically enough to implement. |
142	| **Alternatives considered** | What else was evaluated and why it was rejected. |
143	| **Accessibility impact** | Who benefits and how — named groups, not "users". |
144	| **Risks and tradeoffs** | What was sacrificed, and why that was acceptable. |
145	| **Evidence** | The testing, research, or WCAG criterion supporting it. |
146	
147	Plus the four deferral fields this skill requires on top: severity, **who is excluded** (named groups), **severity of exclusion** — blocked or friction — and a **remediation deadline** (critical: this sprint · major: 30 days · minor: 90 days) with a **review date**.
148	
149	Store it alongside the code where it travels with the implementation. *Never only in someone's head or in a chat thread* — documentation is the immune system that protects a good decision from being undone by someone who doesn't know why it was made.
150	
151	## Folding a HIGH: mandatory tradeoff analysis
152	
153	A `HIGH` finding is never quietly downgraded. If one is going to be accepted rather than fixed, it is folded **by name**, through this analysis, and the result goes in the debt ledger in the format above (`inclusive/tradeoff-analysis`). Six questions:
154	
155	1. **Who benefits from option A?** Which groups gain, roughly how many, and how severe the barrier is without it.
156	2. **Who benefits from option B?** The same analysis for the alternative.
157	3. **Who is harmed by each?** Which groups lose access or degrade, how badly, and whether the harm is permanent or temporary.
158	4. **What is the severity asymmetry?** **Blocked beats friction** — a user who *cannot* complete the task is more severely affected than one for whom it is *harder*, and blockers get removed before friction gets reduced. Permanent conditions outrank situational ones, because a situational user has other options and a permanent user may not.
159	5. **What is the reversibility?** Reversible → take the faster option and schedule the improvement. Irreversible → take the more inclusive option and accept the delay.
160	6. **What is the precedent?** A shortcut taken once becomes the standard unless it is documented as an exception.
161	
162	**Red lines — tradeoffs that are never made:** never ship a feature that is entirely inaccessible by keyboard; never deprioritise a fix that blocks task completion; never treat "we'll fix it later" as acceptable without a tracked item and a date.
163	
164	**The one crossed red line, and why it does not generalise.** Upstream's fourth red line is *"never remove existing accessibility to meet a deadline"*, and **F-011 crossed it deliberately** — motion-sensitivity users lost an opt-out they previously had. It is exempt not because the rule is wrong but because it was crossed the way this section demands: analysed, named, attested by the decision owner in writing, permanent rather than a deadline expedient, and recorded with its cost stated (`design-catalogue/FEEDBACK.md` F-011). That is the bar. **An attested override is a decision; an unattested one is the red line.** Nothing else in this skill inherits the exemption, and F-011 does not widen by analogy to any other preference.
165	
166	## Cheapest fix ladder
167	
168	When more than one fix would work, propose the earliest step that does:
169	
170	1. **Delete** — the decorative layer eating clicks, the ARIA a native element makes redundant, the ramp nothing needs.
171	2. **Use the platform** — the native element or control instead of a custom rebuild.
172	3. **Reuse what the project has** — an existing token, focus style, or spacing step.
173	4. **Correct the value** — the exact contrast pair, hit-area size, or WCAG-conformant markup.
174	5. **Add** — a new token, wrapper, or ARIA attribute only the platform truly cannot supply.
175	
176	A fix proposed at step 5 where step 1 was available is itself a finding.
177	
178	## Never Approve coverage you did not inspect
179	
180	If the target was a screenshot, say keyboard and screen-reader findings are inferred. If a script failed to run, say so and mark that check `Not verified` — never let a tool failure silently read as a pass.
181	
182	## The 30/50/20 testing pyramid
183	
184	Automated tools (axe, this skill's scripts) catch roughly 30% of real barriers — the mechanical ones. Manual expert testing (tab-through, screen-reader pass, zoom, plain-language read) catches another 50%. The remaining 20% — real-world usability barriers, unexpected workarounds, cognitive and emotional friction — surfaces only in testing with actual disabled users. This skill covers the first two layers rigorously; recommend the third to the user rather than claiming it was done.
185	
186	## Before you finish
187	
188	| Mistake | Fix |
189	| --- | --- |
190	| Claiming a script pass without running it against `tests/a11y/broken.html` first | Run the CARL check once per project before trusting any clean result |
191	| Reporting a keyboard or screen-reader finding from a static screenshot | Mark it inferred, not verified — say so in the coverage table |
192	| Averaging an escalation-trigger finding down because the surface is minor | Escalation triggers are `HIGH` on sight, never re-scored |
193	| A finding with no WCAG criterion cited | Look it up in `compliance-mapping`'s tables before writing the row |
194	| Silently dropping a Minor finding not in this fix round | Append it to `.impeccable/a11y-debt.md` with severity, owner, and deadline |
195	| Fixing contrast by changing hue | Change lightness — it's the channel contrast responds to; remeasure after |
196	| Reporting "not accessible" with no persona named | Name who specifically is blocked and what they were trying to do |
197	| Treating four personas with the same permanent disability as full persona coverage | Span permanent, temporary, and situational — 4–6 personas, not a single category |
198	| Proposing a step-5 fix (new ARIA, new token) where step 1–4 would work | Walk the cheapest-fix ladder before proposing an addition |
199	| A colour-only status indicator passed because the label happened to be nearby | Run the greyscale test explicitly and report the result |
200	| `Approve` issued on a domain never actually inspected | Mark that domain `Not reviewed` in the coverage table instead |
201	| An accessibility-debt item deferred with no deadline or owner | Every debt entry needs severity, WCAG criterion, remediation deadline, and explicit user acknowledgement — written in the eight-field ADR shape, not as a one-liner |
202	| A `HIGH` accepted rather than fixed, with no analysis behind it | Run the six tradeoff questions, name who is excluded and whether they are blocked or merely slowed, and record it with a review date |
203	| Landmarks and `<iframe title>` never checked because no script reports them | Read the markup: four landmarks minimum, a title on every frame. `a11y_scan.py` catches `region` and `landmark-one-main`; the frame title and the label on a repeated landmark it does not |
204

1	# Accessibility principle catalog
2	
3	One line per principle, deduplicated by meaning, grouped by the eight audit passes in `SKILL.md`. Source tag in brackets after each line. Source index at the end lists every upstream file, relative to `references/upstream` in the design skill.
4	
5	## Pass 1 — Mechanical
6	
7	- Most accessibility is free if you use the platform; prefer the platform default over a custom rebuild, and remove ARIA rather than add it. [better-accessibility]
8	- A screenshot you didn't read doesn't count, and neither does a check whose output you didn't read. [design/SKILL.md]
9	- CARL rule: before trusting a load-bearing check's clean pass, run it against a version known to be broken and confirm it actually fails. [design/SKILL.md]
10	- Automated tools catch roughly 30% of real barriers, manual expert testing another 50%, testing with disabled users the remaining 20%. [inclusive/accessibility-testing-strategy]
11	- Automated tools miss whether alt text is meaningful, whether focus order is logical, and whether interactions actually work — only a human judges those. [inclusive/accessibility-testing-strategy]
12	- Test priority order: core tasks first, then input and navigation, then content and comprehension, then edge cases and preferences. [inclusive/accessibility-testing-strategy]
13	- Tab from the browser address bar through the entire page and document unreachable elements, wrong order, invisible focus, and traps. [inclusive/keyboard-review]
14	- Audit across devices and browsers, in both static and interactive states. [designer-skills/accessibility-audit]
15	- Believing work is done is not verification; run the check and report the observed result. [designpowers/verification-before-shipping]
16	
17	## Pass 2 — POUR (WCAG 2.2 AA)
18	
19	- POUR: every finding maps to Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, or Robust. [designer-skills/accessibility-audit]
20	- `<button>` for actions, `<a href>` for navigation, never `<div onClick>` — a real link supports Cmd/Ctrl/middle-click. [better-accessibility]
21	- The five rules of ARIA: prefer native semantics, don't change native semantics needlessly, every ARIA control must be fully keyboard-operable, never hide a focusable element, every interactive element needs an accessible name. [better-accessibility/semantics-and-aria]
22	- Accessible-name precedence: `aria-labelledby` > `aria-label` > native label/text/`alt` > `title`. [better-accessibility/semantics-and-aria]
23	- Label in Name (WCAG 2.5.3): the visible label text must appear in the accessible name, or voice-control users saying the visible word can't activate the control. [better-accessibility/semantics-and-aria]
24	- Multiple landmarks of the same type need distinguishing labels, e.g. `<nav aria-label="Primary">`. [better-accessibility/semantics-and-aria]
25	- Native `disabled` removes a control from the tab order and blocks activation; `aria-disabled="true"` keeps it focusable and hoverable for a tooltip. Never set both on one element. [better-accessibility/semantics-and-aria]
26	- Never disable a submit button — keep it enabled, validate on submit, focus the first error. [better-accessibility/semantics-and-aria]
27	- `.sr-only` needs a 1px box, not zero size, plus `white-space: nowrap` — some screen readers skip zero-sized elements. [better-accessibility/screen-readers]
28	- Choose the announcement mechanism in order: focus move, then `aria-describedby` tied to a control, then a polite live region (`role="status"`), then `role="alert"` for urgent untied errors only. [better-accessibility/screen-readers]
29	- A repeated polite live region must be a stable empty region rendered before its text changes, never re-inserted already holding content. [better-accessibility/screen-readers]
30	- `aria-hidden="true"` removes the whole subtree from assistive tech; never place it on or above a focusable element. [better-accessibility/screen-readers]
31	- Alt text by purpose: decorative `alt=""`, informative describes the meaning, functional describes the action, image-of-text reproduces the text, complex gets short alt plus a nearby full description. [better-accessibility/screen-readers]
32	- A missing `alt` is worse than an empty one — screen readers fall back to reading the filename. [better-accessibility/screen-readers]
33	- `aria-invalid="true"` on the failing field, removed once fixed; `aria-describedby` links the field to its inline error text. [better-accessibility/forms]
34	- `autocomplete` with a meaningful `name` is a WCAG 1.3.5 requirement for any field about the user. [better-accessibility/forms]
35	- Never block paste in a field — users paste passwords and one-time codes. [better-accessibility/forms]
36	- Modals trap and restore focus: `inert` on the background content, focus moves in on open, returns to the trigger on close. [better-accessibility]
37	- Map every design decision to its WCAG 2.2 success criterion before it ships, not after an audit finds it. [compliance-mapping]
38	- WCAG 2.2 AA is the global baseline most laws reference; some AAA criteria — especially cognitive ones — are worth adopting even when not required. [compliance-mapping]
39	- Placeholder text is never a label — it disappears on focus and usually fails contrast. [inclusive/form-labelling]
40	- Group related fields with `<fieldset>`/`<legend>` — always for radio groups. [inclusive/form-labelling]
41	- Every table needs `<th scope="col">`/`scope="row"` headers and a `<caption>` describing its content — never "Table 1". [inclusive/table-accessibility]
42	- Don't use tables for layout; use them only for data with a real row/column relationship. [inclusive/table-accessibility]
43	
44	## Pass 3 — Cognitive (COGA)
45	
46	- Three loads: intrinsic (inherent to the task — reduce by chunking, not deletion), extraneous (added by poor design — eliminate ruthlessly), germane (the user's real engagement — maximise by removing the other two). [COGA]
47	- Users must answer "where am I / where can I go / how do I get back" in under a second, without relying on memory. [inclusive/wayfinding-navigation]
48	- Important actions reachable in 1–2 clicks; favour breadth over depth in navigation hierarchies. [inclusive/wayfinding-navigation]
49	- Rate each screen on decisions required, items to remember, new concepts, steps, reading complexity, visual complexity — any dimension rated High means redesign before launch. [inclusive/cognitive-load-assessment]
50	- Map cognitive load across a whole journey to find load spikes and memory bridges, not just isolated screens. [inclusive/assess-load]
51	- Working memory holds roughly 4 items; if the system can remember it, the user shouldn't have to. [inclusive/memory-load-reduction]
52	- Never re-ask information the system already has; pre-fill from earlier steps or sessions. [inclusive/memory-load-reduction]
53	- Auto-save progress in any flow longer than 3 steps; never require starting over when a session expires. [inclusive/memory-load-reduction]
54	- One primary action per screen; secondary actions visually de-emphasised. [inclusive/focus-attention-design]
55	- No autoplaying audio or video, no unsolicited pop-ups; closing a modal never loses the user's work. [inclusive/focus-attention-design]
56	- Avoid time limits; where unavoidable, warn well before expiry and allow one-click extension. [inclusive/focus-attention-design]
57	- Accept multiple date and phone formats, auto-format as the user types, trim whitespace automatically. [inclusive/error-prevention-recovery]
58	- Never clear user input on error — always preserve their work. [inclusive/error-prevention-recovery]
59	- Every error message answers what happened, why, and what to do now — never blames the user. [inclusive/error-prevention-recovery]
60	- Undo available for at least 10 seconds after any action; destructive confirmations state the concrete consequence, not a generic "are you sure?". [inclusive/error-prevention-recovery]
61	- Help must be reachable without leaving the screen the user is stuck on, and never require a reference number to reach a human. [inclusive/contextual-help-design]
62	- Write help content at grade 4–6 reading level, using the same terminology as the interface. [inclusive/contextual-help-design]

64	## Pass 4 — Content
65	
66	- Aim for a reading age of 12–14 (grade 6–8); grade 4–6 for buttons, labels, and errors. [designpowers/accessible-content]
67	- One idea per sentence, active voice, specific over vague — "Save your changes" not "Submit". [designpowers/accessible-content]
68	- Error messages follow "what happened + what to do", placed adjacent to the field, announced via live region or focus move. [designpowers/accessible-content]
69	- People scan before they read — inverted pyramid, most important information first, chunked into short paragraphs. [inclusive/readable-content]
70	- Maximum 3–4 sentences per paragraph; a new heading every 2–3 paragraphs. [inclusive/readable-content]
71	- The 5-second test: can someone read a sentence and understand it in 5 seconds? If not, rewrite. [inclusive/plain-language-design]
72	- Passive voice hides who does what — "Your application has been rejected" hides both the actor and the next step. [inclusive/plain-language-design]
73	- One H1 per page, no skipped levels, headings describe content rather than serving as visual styling. [inclusive/heading-structure]
74	- A screen-reader user scanning only headings should understand the page's structure. [inclusive/heading-structure]
75	- Alt text answers "if this image disappeared, what information would be lost" — not what the image looks like. [inclusive/alt-text-design]
76	- The same image needs different alt text in different contexts. [inclusive/alt-text-design]
77	- Every link makes sense read completely on its own, outside any surrounding sentence. [inclusive/link-text-design]
78	- Same link text must always go to the same destination; different destinations need different text. [inclusive/link-text-design]
79	- File links state type and size; links that open a new tab warn the user first. [inclusive/link-text-design]
80	- Auto-generated captions run 80–85% accuracy — always review and correct before shipping. [inclusive/multimedia-accessibility]
81	- Captions include relevant sound effects and music cues in brackets, not just dialogue. [inclusive/multimedia-accessibility]
82	- Media players need keyboard-accessible controls and speed adjustment (0.5x–2x) — essential for cognitive accessibility. [inclusive/multimedia-accessibility]
83	- Prefer simple tables with one header row; avoid merged cells; give a complex table a text summary. [inclusive/table-accessibility]
84	- Maximum 5–7 columns for comfortable scanning; on small screens convert to a card/list view rather than hiding data. [inclusive/table-accessibility]

87

89	- Identify the actual rendered background — the nearest ancestor that paints one — before measuring, not the page background. [better-colors]
90	- Fix a failing contrast pair by moving lightness, holding hue and saturation — hue and saturation barely move the measured value. [better-colors]
91	- Report a failing pair and its measured value; never repaint without being asked — contrast is a design decision. [better-colors]
92	- A translucent surface's contrast shifts with whatever scrolls behind it — test against the lightest and darkest content it can sit over. [better-colors]

95	- `forced-colors: active` strips authored colour — borders and outlines must still define interactive elements without it. [inclusive/user-preference-respect]
96	- 1 in 12 male users has colour vision deficiency; colour can enhance meaning but must never be its only carrier. [inclusive/colour-independence]

103	- A simplified view is a focused version containing everything needed for core tasks, not a stripped-down "lite" mode. [inclusive/simplified-views]

[better-accessibility/motion-and-zoom]

106	- Test realistic preference combinations together — dark mode plus high contrast — not each in isolation; reduced motion is no longer part of that combination to test. [inclusive/preference-audit]

108	## Pass 6 — Interaction
109	
110	- Style `:focus-visible`, never bare `:focus`; prefer the browser's unmodified ring, verified against every adjacent colour it crosses. [better-accessibility/focus-and-keyboard]
111	- `tabindex="0"` joins the natural tab order, `tabindex="-1"` is for programmatic focus only, positive values are never acceptable — they hijack the whole page's tab order. [better-accessibility/focus-and-keyboard]
112	- Roving tabindex (a roving `tabindex` pattern) for composite widgets (tabs, menus, toolbars, radio groups): one Tab stop, active item `0`, the rest `-1`, arrow keys move both. [better-accessibility/focus-and-keyboard]
113	- A skip link is the first focusable element, hidden until focused, targeting `<main id="main">`; anchor targets get `scroll-margin-top` so a sticky header never hides them. [better-accessibility/focus-and-keyboard]
114	- SPA route changes must update `document.title` and move focus to the new view's heading or `<main>` — client-side routing resets nothing on its own. [better-accessibility/focus-and-keyboard]
115	- WCAG 2.5.8 AA floor is 24×24 CSS px; 44×44 is the recommended touch target, 40×40 a usable desktop one; the spacing exception allows a smaller target with enough gap around it. [better-accessibility/hit-areas]
116	- Extend the hit area with a pseudo-element on the wrapping label or button, never on the input itself; two extended hit areas must never overlap. [better-accessibility/hit-areas]
117	- Decorative layers (glows, scrims, blurred sheens) get `pointer-events: none` so clicks reach the real control beneath. [better-accessibility/hit-areas]
118	- Every interactive element must be reachable by Tab, in an order matching the visual reading order — no element reachable only by hover or click. [inclusive/keyboard-navigation]
119	- Drag-and-drop always needs a keyboard alternative — move up/down buttons or arrow-key reordering. [inclusive/keyboard-navigation]
120	- Trigger actions on touch-up, not touch-down, so a user can slide away to cancel. [inclusive/touch-target-design]
121	- Separate destructive actions from common ones by distance or visual weight, never adjacent with no gap. [inclusive/touch-target-design]
122	- Every gesture (swipe, pinch, shake, long-press) needs a visible, single-action button alternative — gestures are shortcuts, never gatekeepers. [inclusive/gesture-alternatives]
123	- Build the button-based version first, add gesture support as an enhancement on top — that ordering guarantees the alternative always exists. [inclusive/gesture-alternatives]
124	- Every action must be possible through at least keyboard and pointer; never lock a feature to one input method. [inclusive/multi-modal-input]
125	- Never disable paste in a text field — password managers and assistive tools depend on it. [inclusive/multi-modal-input]
126	- Every piece of feedback works through at least two channels (visual plus text, minimum); colour alone is never one of the two. [inclusive/feedback-and-status]
127	- Transient toasts show for at least 5 seconds and never carry the only path to an action; errors stay until resolved, never auto-dismiss. [inclusive/feedback-and-status]
128	- Voice is an accelerator, never a gatekeeper — every voice interaction needs a text, touch, or keyboard alternative. [inclusive/voice-interaction]
129	- Never autoplay content with motion — show a static poster first, and give every moving element a visible pause control. [inclusive/motion-sensitivity]
130	
131	## Pass 7 — Persona walkthrough
132	
133	- Nothing About Us Without Us — design for the margins and the centre benefits; design for the centre and the margins get excluded. [designpowers/inclusive-personas]
134	- Build 4–6 personas: 2–3 primary users, 1–2 edge-case users, 1 stress-case user. [designpowers/inclusive-personas]
135	- Accessibility is a spectrum, not binary — map where each core task degrades from "works" to "fails" and for whom, rather than a single pass/fail. [inclusive/ability-spectrum-mapping]
136	- Weave disability into the full persona — goals, frustrations, context — never as an isolated "accessibility persona" pulled out only when someone remembers it. [inclusive/disability-inclusive-personas]
137	- Minimum diversity rule for any set of 4+: at least one permanent disability, at least one situational impairment, a range of technical confidence. [inclusive/disability-inclusive-personas]
138	- Every user is impaired in the right context — bright sunlight, a noisy commute, one hand holding a child — and the fixes that help them also help permanent-disability users. [inclusive/situational-impairment-mapping]
139	- Name the actual assistive technology and describe the interaction step by step, not just the disability and the goal. [inclusive/assistive-technology-scenarios]
140	- "That's an edge case" is the most common way accessibility gets deprioritised — if it affects disabled users, it's a design requirement, not an exception. [inclusive/edge-case-identification]
141	- Invert every happy-path assumption: desktop to mobile/screen reader, fast internet to offline, sees colour to colour-blind, one sitting to interrupted and resumed days later. [inclusive/edge-case-identification]
142	- Build accessibility into every story's acceptance criteria — keyboard, screen reader, visual, motor, cognitive — never a separate "accessibility ticket". [inclusive/inclusive-user-stories]
143	- Prioritise scenarios where the highest-risk task meets the most-affected persona, not an even sweep of every combination. [inclusive/scenario-map]
144	- Cognitive walkthrough per task: will the user try the right action, notice it, associate it with the right effect, and see that progress was made? Any "no" is a finding. [designpowers/heuristic-evaluator]
145	
146	## Pass 8 — Report and decisions
147	
148	- Escalation triggers are HIGH the moment confirmed, never averaged down because the surface is minor. [better-interface]
149	- The bar for reporting is evidence, not taste; a trigger fails regardless of the style guide, and a preference merely disagreed with is not a finding. [better-interface]
150	- Consolidate one root cause into one row, listing every location it reaches — never pad a report to fill a cap. [better-interface]
151	- `Approve` claims the coverage actually inspected; never issue it for a domain not checked. [better-interface]
152	- Accessibility debt compounds: new features build on an inaccessible foundation and inherit its inaccessibility; the longer an issue persists, the more code grows around it. [inclusive/accessibility-debt-tracking]
153	- Triage by deadline: critical fixes this sprint, major within 30 days, minor within 90 days; anything past its deadline escalates automatically. [inclusive/accessibility-debt-tracking]
154	- A previously fixed issue that reappears is a regression — treat it as critical by default, not as a fresh minor finding. [inclusive/accessibility-debt-tracking]
155	- EAA (in force since June 2025) and EN 301 549 align with WCAG 2.1 AA plus extra software, hardware, and documentation requirements; ADA and Section 508 case law both reference WCAG. [compliance-mapping]
156	- Record context, the decision, alternatives considered, who benefits, and the risks accepted — so a future redesign doesn't undo a deliberate accessibility choice by accident. [inclusive/decision-documentation]
157	- A user who cannot complete a task (blocked) is more severely affected than one who finds it merely harder (friction) — prioritise removing blockers. [inclusive/tradeoff-analysis]
158	- Never ship a feature completely inaccessible by keyboard, and never remove existing accessibility to meet a deadline — these are red lines, not tradeoffs to weigh. [inclusive/tradeoff-analysis]
159	- Match the accessibility argument to who's listening: risk and revenue for leadership, conversion and scope for product, specific criteria for engineers, craft quality for designers. [inclusive/stakeholder-communication]
160	- Plan a testing strategy across all three pyramid layers — automated, manual expert, real disabled users — not just the automated one. [inclusive/accessibility-testing-strategy]
161	- Before declaring done: check the debt register, confirm critical and major items are resolved (not just open), and get explicit user acknowledgement for anything accepted as debt. [designpowers/verification-before-shipping]
162	- On a review of an existing artefact, build a lightweight inferred brief (key task, audience across the ability spectrum, quality bar) rather than skipping straight to findings. [designpowers/design-review]
163	- Reconciliation order when reviewers disagree: accessibility over aesthetics, usability over style, brief over opinion, personas break ties, escalate to the user only if still unresolved. [designpowers/using-designpowers]
164	- Classify every finding critical/major/minor, name who is affected, and give a specific fix, not a vague direction. [designpowers/accessibility-reviewer]
165	- Distinguish issues that block shipping from improvements for a future iteration; acknowledge what works before listing what doesn't. [designpowers/design-critic]
166	
167	## Source index
168	
169	Paths are relative to `references/upstream` in the `design` skill.

171	- `interfaces/skills/better-accessibility/`: SKILL.md, focus-and-keyboard.md, forms.md, hit-areas.md, motion-and-zoom.md, screen-readers.md, semantics-and-aria.md
172	- `interfaces/skills/better-interface/`: SKILL.md, review-format.md
173	- `interfaces/skills/better-colors/`: SKILL.md (contrast section)
174	- `designpowers/agents/`: accessibility-reviewer.md, design-critic.md, heuristic-evaluator.md
175	- `designpowers/skills/`: accessible-content/SKILL.md, cognitive-accessibility/SKILL.md, adaptive-interfaces/SKILL.md, inclusive-personas/SKILL.md, verification-before-shipping/SKILL.md, design-review/SKILL.md, using-designpowers/SKILL.md (Reconciliation Protocol section only)

177	- `inclusive/accessibility-decisions/skills/`: accessibility-debt-tracking, accessibility-testing-strategy, compliance-mapping, decision-documentation, document, handoff, review, stakeholder-communication, tradeoff-analysis (each `/SKILL.md`)
178	- `inclusive/accessible-content/skills/`: alt-text-design, form-labelling, heading-structure, link-text-design, multimedia-accessibility, readable-content, review, rewrite, structure, table-accessibility (each `/SKILL.md`)
179	- `inclusive/adaptive-interfaces/skills/`: colour-independence, flexible-typography, information-density, preference-audit, responsive-accessibility, responsive-review, simplified-views, specify, user-preference-respect (each `/SKILL.md`)
180	- `inclusive/cognitive-accessibility/skills/`: assess-load, cognitive-load-assessment, contextual-help-design, error-prevention-recovery, focus-attention-design, memory-load-reduction, plain-language-design, review, simplify, wayfinding-navigation (each `/SKILL.md`). Upstream also ships an

## Design Read (en rad)

Lågexponerad gråskalescen i registret `cinematic dark` och grammatiken `continuous world`:
ett enda visitkort ligger på ett bord under en snedställd lampa och vänds medan besökaren
scrollar, med rubriken stilla utanför kortet i affischgrad.

Kategorin är `portfolio` med `product-focused` som andrakategori, båda låsta av
`BRIEF-draft.md` och bekräftade av `select.py`s egen poängrad (`+3 register | +3 grammatik
| +2 category2` på `oryzo-ai`).

## Dial-deklaration

Arkitektens tre riktvärden behålls oförändrade. Ingen avvikelse.

| Ratt | Siffra | En mening |
|---|---|---|
| **variance** | **4** | Grammatik, nav, värld, palett och typsnitt är oförändrade från V3b och tre dimensioner ändras av ett och samma ingrepp, att plåten blir ett kort med två sidor; en femma skulle ha krävt ett nytt hero-motiv och en trea vore ren polering. |
| **motion** | **7** | En pinnad akt bär hela toppen med en kontinuerlig bespoke-rotation och tre andra ställen kör bespoke paint, men sex av sju skärmar är `flow` med kort stagger, det finns noll scrub-akter och ingen andra `pin`. |
| **density** | **3** | Sju skärmar, ett displayelement per skärm, liggarrader i stället för kort, högst fyra monoetiketter på hela sidan, och två hela sektioner tas bort utan att ersättas av något nytt. |

## Reference lock (7 fält)

```text
Primary reference/direction: tests/alunix-concepts-r5/cells/V3b-chain/index.html — den låsta
  byggnad V3c itererar. reference-lock.md, Tier 0: "Primary = the locked system itself."
Preserve: kontinuerlig svartvit fotografisk grund (k4-cabin-desk.webp) med --sc-canvas-drift
  i tre stopp; R5-världen vänster (Geist, #0b0c0e/#1e5e9c) och R6-världen höger (Public Sans,
  #fdfbf4); rubriken utanför plåten i affischskala; Hyperborea-plåten som bleeder förbi sin
  egen kant; ordscrubben i liggaren; Calyx och Hōrai live i iframe, aldrig transformerade
  efter att de visats.
Borrow only: (1) oryzo-ai — ett fysiskt objekt som vrider sig i ett mörkt tomrum, där
  materialet och kanten under ett snedljus är det som gör rotationen läsbar. (2) mattis-studio
  — konsolkortet, lånat som AVVISNING: V3c:s kort är ett fysiskt kort med två sidor, inte en
  ritad ram med hörnmarkeringar, versionstagg och klocka.
Role rules: #1e5e9c gör exakt en sak och förekommer exakt två gånger på sidan (tesplåtens
  grund inklusive dess drift-mål #123f68, och understrykningen i "Boka ett möte ->"); aldrig
  ram, aldrig knappfyllning, aldrig i liggaren. Geist Mono är enbart register, max fyra
  monoetiketter på hela sidan. Public Sans 300 är enbart display och brödtext. Rollerna
  korsar aldrig. Hårlinje `--frame-line` är plåtens enda kant; radie 0 överallt.
Media strategy: product surface (Calyx, Hōrai och Hyperborea är byråns egna, live eller
  skärmbild) + vendored grayscale still (grunden och hero-plåten, ärvda ur r5, se
  assets/ASSETS.md). Enum, ett värde per plats. INTE photo:unsplash, INTE generated.
Reject: glaskort och konsol-chrome (F-006); ritad webbläsar- eller telefonram (gate 47);
  fabricerad produkt-UI (gate 79); scroll-cue-text (gate 88); tidsstämpel eller
  "2026 · SVERIGE" på kortbaksidan; en andra lede i folden; tre lika tjänstekort;
  logotypvägg, omdömen, betyg, kundantal, år i branschen; en andra accent; skugga.
Token commitments: canvas #0b0c0e; paper #fdfbf4; accent #1e5e9c (ett bruk, två förekomster);
  thesis drift #123f68; hairline --frame-line; radie 0 (skalan {0-3}); pricing: ledger
  (hårlinjerader, display-siffror); services: numbered ledger 01-03, aldrig kort;
  display Public Sans 300 ~130px hero / Geist 700 ~81px kortbaksida; body 16px; register
  Geist Mono 10.5px, tracking .22em.
```

## Decision ledger

En rad per materiellt val. Ett val utan rad skeppas inte.

| Area | Decision | Source | Source rule | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Palett** | `#0b0c0e` grund, `#fdfbf4` papper, `#1e5e9c` accent; inget nytt val görs | Målbilden (planens § 7.5) + V3b:s eget lås | TASTE § 4.4, ett papper och en accent som gör en sak | V3c är en iteration; att öppna paletten vore ett nytt bygge |
| **Accentens frekvens** | `#1e5e9c` förekommer exakt två gånger: tesplåtens grund och understrykningen i `Boka ett möte ->` | Katalogposten `dope-security` § What to borrow | "State an accent's frequency as a number, not a feeling" | Ett tal är granskningsbart; "sparsamt" är det inte |
| **Typ** | Geist (röst + kortbaksida), Geist Mono (register), Public Sans 300 (display + brödtext); rollerna korsar aldrig | Målbilden + V3b | TASTE § 4.2, två snitt och rollerna korsar aldrig | Ärvt från en godkänd cell; `brand.md`:s fyra steg körs inte om |
| **Nav** | Tunn topprad med ordmärke och kontakt som scrollar bort; oförändrad från V3b | V3b:s registerrad | `feel-and-fingerprint.md` dimension 2 | Nav är en av de tre dimensioner som INTE ändras, vilket är vad som gör V3c till en iteration |
| **Hero-device** | `section.hero` blir `data-sc-act="pin" data-sc-span="2.2" data-sc-dwell="0.35"`; motorns stage-markup ur `template.html`, aldrig restylade `.sc-*`-klasser | Målbilden | AB06, motorn redigeras aldrig | Vändningen behöver scrollrum som en `flow`-akt inte har |
| **Aktform** | Sju skärmar: en pinnad akt plus sex flow; `panel-open` och `panel-services` tas bort | Målbilden | TASTE § 5 (tre lika kort) och F-006 | Konsolkortets innehåll bor nu på kortbaksidan; tjänstepanelen dubblerade liggaren |
| **Avslut** | Prisliggaren och `kontakt@alunix.se` som en typsatt rad; inget formulär, ingen sticky CTA | r7 § Alunix, fakta | "inget formulär som skickar någonstans" | Rut-testet: kategorins default är ett formulär i botten |
| **Memorable detail** | Kortet vänds: `--flip = smoothstep(0.12, 0.72, --sc-ps)` driver `rotateY` på `.plate-card`, framsidan är fotografisk, baksidan matt svart med ordmärket | `oryzo-ai` (objektet som vrider sig i tomrum), omtolkat till Alunix eget visitkort | `reference-lock.md`: Memorable detail-raden är obligatorisk | Rubriken säger "nutidens visitkort"; sidan låter besökaren vända det |
| **Hero-plåtens stillbild** | Omtagning av hero-plattan utgår -> koreografin ändras så att den bild som finns bär flippen (`assets/ASSETS.md` § 3 väg (d)) · Källa: planens § 10.6 fallback steg 3 · Orsak: Higgsfield 0 credits, free plan, mätt 2026-09-09 av lead | Planens § 10.6 steg 3 | "byt deviceform, aldrig kvaliteten" | F-007-kontrollen visade att ljuspölen inte bär flippen; två rena opacity-tillägg löser två av tre skäl utan att importera ett nytt motiv |
| **Rörelsens datakälla** | Allt som förflyttar sig läser `--sc-ps`; cue-opacitet och drift-ton får läsa `--sc-p` | F-014 punkt 1 | `motion-smoothness.md` § The rule | V3b:s bespoke rörelse läste rå `--sc-p` och stegade (staircase 9 och 16) |
| **Prestanda** | Se § Prestandaplan nedan; varje post i F-013 har ett målvärde | F-013 + `performance.md` § 1 | Gate 93 | V3b sköt 4,9 MB, 19 typsnittsfiler och 17 långa tasks |

### Byggarens rader, R1

En rad per ytterligare materiellt val. Fem av dem är rättelser av något som V3b faktiskt
gör i dag och som bryter mot ett lås i den här filen; de är markerade **rättelse**.

| Area | Decision | Source | Source rule | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Accenttalet, rättelse 1** | `.thread-fill` (liggarens självritande tråd) byter från `var(--c-accent)` till `var(--c-ink)` i 2 px mot 1 px `--c-line-on-paper` | Reference lock § Role rules i den här filen | "aldrig i liggaren" | V3b ritar tråden i `#1e5e9c`. Det är accentens tredje förekomst och den ligger precis där låset förbjuder den. Värdekontrast i stället för kulörkontrast håller kvar V3b:s runda 2-fynd att tråden ska läsa som ett ritverktyg, inte som en ram |
| **Accenttalet, rättelse 2** | Fokusringen slutar vara `--c-accent`. Två värden, ett per grund: `#f4f2ef` på den mörka grunden, `#16140f` på papperet, 2 px, offset 2 px | `house-physics.md` "Every muted tone needs a value per ground" + WCAG 1.4.11 | Icke-textkontrast >= 3:1 | Mätt: `#1e5e9c` mot `#0b0c0e` ger **2,93:1** och underkänns; mot `#fdfbf4` ger 6,46:1. `#f4f2ef` mot `#0b0c0e` ger **17,5:1**. Fixen tar samtidigt bort accentens fjärde förekomst |
| **Accenttalet, kvarvarande** | Efter de två raderna ovan förekommer `#1e5e9c` exakt två gånger: tesplåtens grund (med `#123f68` som dess drift-mål, samma roll) och understrykningen i `Boka ett möte →` | `dope-security` § What to borrow | "State an accent's frequency as a number, not a feeling" | Talet är nu granskningsbart mot koden och inte bara mot avsikten. Motorns egen `--sc-accent` räknas inte: inget synligt element läser den |
| **Hero-rubrikens skala, rättelse 3** | `.hero-headline`s tak höjs från `7rem` till `7.5rem`; `.plate-card`s `ALUNIX` behåller `clamp(3.2rem, 9cqw, 7.5rem)` | `concepts-V3c.md` (1), måltalen kvot <= 0,70 och baksida >= 5x brödtext | TASTE § 1 och § 2.4 | Aritmetiken går inte ihop med V3b:s eget tak. Vid 1440 är `9cqw` av sidcontainern 129,6 px men `7rem` = **112 px** binder, så rubriken renderar 112 px och inte de ~130 px `concepts-V3c.md` räknar med. Baksidan blir `9cqw` av plåtens 896 px = **80,6 px**. Kvoten blir **0,72**, över taket 0,70. Att i stället sänka baksidan bryter 5x-golvet (5 x 16 px = 80 px). `7.5rem` = 120 px ger kvot **0,67** och baksidan **5,04x** brödtexten, och kostar 16 px extra höjd i en fold som mäter ~823 px av 900 |

Utan den här raden mäter `9cqw` mot 1440 och baksidans ordmärke renderar 129,6 px i stället för 80,6 px, alltså större än rubriken. `container-type: inline-size` ger `contain: layout style inline-size` och klipper inget, så `perspective` och `preserve-3d` är opåverkade |
| **Låst copy, rättelse 4** | `Webbdesign, design och system. Allt på ett ställe.` flyttas ordagrant till platsen under `VI BYGGER ERT VARUMÄRKE.` och ersätter V3b:s `.giant-sub` | `PRODUCT.md` § Brand Commitments, listan över låst copy | Copy-gate: bevara, skriv aldrig om | Raden bor i dag inuti `section.panel-services`, som målbilden tar bort. Utan den här raden försvinner en av sidans låsta strängar med sektionen. Den text som ersätts (`En sammanhållen process ... med samma team hela vägen.`) är dessutom påhittad och påstår ett team, vilket `PRODUCT.md` § absences förbjuder |
| **Borttagen copy, rättelse 5** | `panel-open`s brödtext (`Vi designar och bygger webbplatser, i nära dialog med verksamheten som ska leva i dem.`) återinförs inte någonstans | Målbilden: "Ingen tidsstämpel, ingen `2026 · SVERIGE`, ingen lede" | En lede i folden, inte två | Den försvinner med `panel-open` och underraden under plåten bär redan leden |
| **Cue-kontraktet i heron** | Heron får ingen `data-sc-cue`. Rubrik, plåt och underrad är stagens ground och är synliga från p = 0 | `scroll/devices.md` § The cue contract, "Ground or greet" | Gate 88 | Kravet är uppfyllt via ground, inte via en greet-cue, och därför behövs ingen cue-text alls |
| **Flow direkt efter pinnen** | `.stagger` får `padding-top: 0` på desktop; seamen mellan hero och första panelen bärs av `.col > * + *`-gapet | `scroll/devices.md` § The premium fade-in, sista stycket | "A flow section directly after a pinned act takes reduced padding" | Pinnens spacer tar redan en hel viewport att scrolla bort; V3b:s `clamp(28px,4.6vw,56px)` ovanpå den lägger en halvtom skärm till som `scroll_verify.py` inte kallar dead scroll men som läsaren ser |
| **Iframe-montering** | `loading="lazy"` plus IntersectionObserver med `rootMargin: 100% 0px` som sätter `src` först vid montering; ingen `transform` och ingen `opacity` på ramen eller någon förfader efter att den visats | `performance.md` § 2 Iframes + `PRODUCT.md` § Operating Context | "An iframe mounted at load" står på Never-listan | Två live-ramar monterade vid load är den enskilt tyngsta posten i F-013:s 4,9 MB.
